a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT treat the existing verification reports as authoritative. They are intermediate verification artifacts and must themselves be checked against the source corpus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames the entire session: chronological/document evolution across ~200 steps in phase_measure_theory is itself evidence that must be reconstructed; existing verification reports are intermediate artifacts, not authoritative, and must themselves be re-checked against the primary source corpus. The objective is not to assess whether the latest document looks plausible but to reconstruct and verify the complete evolution from Step 1 through Step 200 and establish whether every important surviving claim has a traceable, justified path from its source through development into the final theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every step, determine: 1. What was proposed? ... 17. If the idea remains unresolved, is that explicitly represented as unresolved?
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 17-question per-step extraction protocol: what was proposed, what motivated it, definitions introduced, mathematical claims, assumptions, objections/contradictions identified, whether the idea was modified/rejected/superseded, whether it was experimentally tested and whether that test was actually executed or merely proposed, which later document addresses it, its final surviving form, where that form appears in current documentation, whether an absence is intentional or a documentation gap, whether a transformed appearance is justified, and whether unresolved status is explicitly represented as such.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "this is now the revised definition" does NOT make that definition verified ... "tested" does NOT mean the test was actually executed ... programme/process status is evidence about the development process, not mathematical proof.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and applies the existing verification rule that programme/process status is evidence about the development process, not mathematical proof: labels such as 'revised', 'frozen', 'PASS', 'ratified', 'tested', or 'canonical' appearing in a document do not by themselves establish that a definition is verified, mathematically proven, experimentally executed, mathematically sound, or that canonicality has been demonstrated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### A. Senior Mathematician ... ### B. Senior Statistician ... Explicitly distinguish: defined -> mathematically valid -> statistically justified -> empirically validated. ### C. Senior DDD / Enterprise Architect ... Verify whether the mathematical concepts and the DDD concepts actually refer to the same things.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the verifier to simultaneously hold three role-based checklists: (A) a senior-mathematician checklist covering definitions, domains/codomains, well-formedness, notation, quantifiers, assumptions, propositions, derivations, proof obligations, existence, uniqueness, consistency, satisfiability, identifiability, computability, convergence, invariance, algebraic properties, probability foundations, statistical validity, measurement theory, and information-theoretic claims, never accepting a formula merely because it looks sophisticated; (B) a senior-statistician checklist (probability-space assumptions, estimands, random variables, distributions, likelihoods, priors, posteriors, sampling, independence, uncertainty propagation, missingness, confidence/credible intervals, calibration, selection bias, identifiability, estimation, statistical decision theory, aggregation, empirical validation) with the explicit ladder defined -> mathematically valid -> statistically justified -> empirically validated; and (C) a senior-DDD/enterprise-architect checklist (bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, aggregates, entities, value objects, domain events, commands, policies, services, authority, responsibilities, state ownership, invariants, domain boundaries, terminology, semantic consistency, architecture implications), whose most important obligation is verifying that mathematical concepts and DDD concepts actually refer to the same things and never allowing a mathematical term and a DDD term to silently acquire different meanings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create: verification/200-step-longitudinal-verification-plan.md ... Create: verification/200-step-traceability-matrix.md ... | Step | Source | Idea / Question | Definition | Derivation | Assumption | Test | Later Resolution | Final Location | Status |
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires two first deliverables before deep verification begins: a 200-step longitudinal verification plan (all discovered documents, their actual logical/document ordering -- not assumed filename ordering -- step number, subject, dependencies, predecessor/successor documents, whether the document introduces/refines/rejects/tests/consolidates theory, expected verification work, relevant existing artifacts, priority, status) and a step traceability matrix with columns Step/Source/Idea-Question/Definition/Derivation/Assumption/Test/Later-Resolution/Final-Location/Status covering all 200 steps, using the marker NO-SURVIVING-THEORY for a step verified to have no lasting theoretical contribution rather than omitting it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Classify every significant statement as one or more of: DEFINITION, AXIOM / POSTULATE, ASSUMPTION, CONJECTURE, PROPOSITION, THEOREM, DERIVATION, EMPIRICAL CLAIM, OBSERVATION, DESIGN CHOICE, POLICY, ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM, DDD CLAIM, OPEN QUESTION, SPECULATION. Never upgrade a weaker category into a stronger one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 14-category epistemic-role classification scheme distinct from the 200-step programme's other vocabularies: DEFINITION, AXIOM/POSTULATE, ASSUMPTION, CONJECTURE, PROPOSITION, THEOREM, DERIVATION, EMPIRICAL CLAIM, OBSERVATION, DESIGN CHOICE, POLICY, ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM, DDD CLAIM, OPEN QUESTION, SPECULATION, with the standing rule that a weaker category may never be silently upgraded into a stronger one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If it defines: K_{t+1} = delta(K_t,e_t) verify: what exactly is K? what exactly is e? what is the domain of delta? is delta total or partial? can delta actually be evaluated?
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates the required mathematical well-formedness check with two worked examples: for a claimed function f: A -> B, verify that A exists, B exists, f is actually defined, every allowed input has an output, and the claimed properties follow; for a claimed transition K_{t+1} = delta(K_t, e_t), verify exactly what K and e are, what delta's domain is, whether delta is total or partial, what its preconditions are, whether delta can actually be evaluated, what information it requires, and what happens when a precondition fails.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use verdicts: DERIVATION_VALID, DERIVATION_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVATION_INCOMPLETE, DERIVATION_INVALID, DERIVATION_NOT_RECONSTRUCTABLE
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires every important derivation to be independently reconstructed (not merely checked for the presence of intermediate equations) as Premises -> transformation -> intermediate result -> conclusion, testing whether each transformation follows, whether hidden assumptions are introduced, whether variables/dimensions/types are compatible, whether quantifiers are preserved, whether boundary conditions are missing, and whether an invoked theorem's conditions are actually satisfied; assigns one of five verdicts: DERIVATION_VALID, DERIVATION_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVATION_INCOMPLETE, DERIVATION_INVALID, DERIVATION_NOT_RECONSTRUCTABLE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Required Inputs -> Available Inputs -> Algorithm -> Output ... Use: COMPUTABLE, COMPUTABLE_CONDITIONAL, COMPUTABLE_BUT_INTRACTABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE_FROM_AVAILABLE_INFORMATION, NOT_YET_ESTABLISHED
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires distinguishing 'algorithmically describable' from 'computable from the available information' for every computational definition, established via the chain Required Inputs -> Available Inputs -> Algorithm -> Output and questions about observability, parameter availability, known distributions, estimable probabilities, identifiable models, finiteness, termination, complexity, reproducibility, and determinism; assigns one of five verdicts: COMPUTABLE, COMPUTABLE_CONDITIONAL, COMPUTABLE_BUT_INTRACTABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE_FROM_AVAILABLE_INFORMATION, NOT_YET_ESTABLISHED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cross-reference the existing A6-statistical-register.md ... Definition -> Assumptions -> Estimand -> Estimator -> Sampling/Observation Model -> Result -> Validation
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires independently re-verifying the existing A6-statistical-register.md against the primary corpus rather than trusting its conclusions, establishing for every statistical formula the chain Definition -> Assumptions -> Estimand -> Estimator -> Sampling/Observation Model -> Result -> Validation, and explicitly flagging nine anti-patterns: probability without probability space, likelihood without likelihood model, posterior without prior, confidence without statistical definition, uncertainty without scale/type, independence without justification, convergence without estimand, estimator without sampling model, and empirical claims without experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create: verification/ubiquitous-language-verification.md ... | Term | First Meaning | Later Meaning | Final Meaning | Same Concept? | DDD Meaning | Mathematical Meaning | Conflict |
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a complete terminology map for at least 35 named terms (Knowledge, Evidence, Observation, Information, Assertion, Assessment, Claim, Proposition, Truth, Belief, Confidence, Uncertainty, State, Knowledge State, System State, Event, Command, Action, Transition, Process, Policy, Authority, Decision, Determination, Validation, Verification, Provenance, Lineage, Context, Conflict, Unknown, Underdetermined, Refuted, Supported, Accepted, Validated), tracking first/later/final meaning, DDD meaning vs mathematical meaning, and whether these are the same concept; requires identifying synonym collisions, overloaded terms, terminology drift, silent renames, meaning changes, math/DDD semantic mismatches, terms in equations absent from the ubiquitous language, and ubiquitous-language terms with no formal definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Origin -> Problem -> Discussion -> Proposed Resolution -> Verification -> Final Status ... Use this when an important earlier question/problem disappears from later documents without an explicit resolution. This is a major finding.
a_rows_sample.statement: For every significant historical issue, requires constructing the chain Origin -> Problem -> Discussion -> Proposed Resolution -> Verification -> Final Status and assigning one of eight statuses: RESOLVED, PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, STILL_OPEN, LOST_IN_EVOLUTION, CONTRADICTED, DOCUMENTATION_GAP. Singles out LOST_IN_EVOLUTION -- an important earlier question/problem that disappears from later documents without any explicit resolution -- as a major finding category in its own right.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every final-theory definition/proposition, trace backwards: Final Theory -> Verification Artifact -> Later Source -> Earlier Source -> Original Motivation ... mark: ORIGIN_NOT_ESTABLISHED ... For every major early theoretical idea trace forward: Original Idea -> Later Development -> Final Treatment
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires both backward traceability (Final Theory -> Verification Artifact -> Later Source -> Earlier Source -> Original Motivation, marking ORIGIN_NOT_ESTABLISHED if a final concept has no historical derivation) and forward traceability (Original Idea -> Later Development -> Final Treatment, classifying each early idea as survived/changed/rejected/replaced/absorbed/remains-unresolved/disappeared), explicitly to prevent the final documentation from presenting a partial history as if it were the complete theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish: TEST_PROPOSED from TEST_EXECUTED from EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED from MATHEMATICALLY_PROVEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: For every claim of TESTED/PASS/VERIFIED/VALIDATED/COMPUTABLE/CONFORMANT/SOUND, requires finding the underlying evidence by asking whether an actual experiment was executed, what the input/procedure/expected/observed results were, whether it is reproducible, and whether passing the test actually establishes the claimed theorem; requires distinguishing TEST_PROPOSED, TEST_EXECUTED, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, and MATHEMATICALLY_PROVEN as four non-interchangeable statuses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Existence Does at least one object/state/model satisfying the definition actually exist? ### Satisfiability Can all declared invariants simultaneously hold? ... The existing observation that the invariant system may be vacuous or unsatisfiable is a high-priority verification target.
a_rows_sample.statement: For every formal model, requires explicitly testing (not assuming) existence -- does at least one object/state/model satisfying the definition actually exist -- and satisfiability -- can all declared invariants simultaneously hold; flags a prior existing observation that the invariant system may be vacuous or unsatisfiable as a high-priority verification target.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identify contradictions between: Step N and Step N+1, early and late definitions, parallel development branches, mathematical theory and DDD model, theory and experiments, theory and final documentation ... Do NOT resolve contradictions by intuition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires cross-step (not merely within-file) contradiction analysis across six axes -- adjacent steps, early vs late definitions, parallel development branches, mathematical theory vs DDD model, theory vs experiments, theory vs final documentation -- recording for each contradiction its two sources, exact claims, semantic interpretation, whether one supersedes the other and the evidence for supersession, and final disposition; explicitly forbids resolving contradictions by intuition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The final theory documentation must be constructed independently from the source corpus plus verified results. Do NOT simply edit the existing final document.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that after the 200-step verification, the final theory documentation must be independently reconstructed via a fixed 12-stage pipeline (source corpus -> 200-step traceability -> definitions -> dependencies -> derivations -> mathematical verification -> statistical verification -> computational verification -> measurement verification -> DDD/ubiquitous-language verification -> architecture verification -> contradictions/gaps -> verified theory), rather than by editing the existing final document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every repair or proposed refinement must be recorded separately as: PROPOSED_REFINEMENT and must never be confused with: SOURCE_CLAIM or VERIFIED_RESULT.
a_rows_sample.statement: Forbids silently repairing an ambiguous definition, silently completing an incomplete derivation, choosing between two conflicting definitions because one looks better, softening a false theorem into a vague statement, or calling an absent experiment tested; every repair or refinement must instead be recorded separately as PROPOSED_REFINEMENT and must never be confused with SOURCE_CLAIM or VERIFIED_RESULT.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum distinguish: PROVEN, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, DEFINITIONALLY_VALID, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, TESTED, TEST_PROPOSED, PLAUSIBLE, CONJECTURED, UNVERIFIED, INCOMPLETE, CONTRADICTED, INVALID, UNDEFINED, NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE, OPEN. Never collapse these categories.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a required 17-item final status vocabulary that must never be collapsed: PROVEN, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, DEFINITIONALLY_VALID, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, TESTED, TEST_PROPOSED, PLAUSIBLE, CONJECTURED, UNVERIFIED, INCOMPLETE, CONTRADICTED, INVALID, UNDEFINED, NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE, OPEN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Follow this order: Phase 1 -- Corpus inventory ... Phase 12 -- Gap and uncertainty report
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a 12-phase research order: (1) corpus inventory, (2) historical reconstruction, (3) step-by-step verification of Steps 1-200, (4) definition reconstruction, (5) derivation reconstruction, (6) mathematical verification, (7) measurement/statistical verification, (8) computational verification, (9) DDD/ubiquitous-language verification, (10) architecture consistency, (11) final theory reconstruction, (12) gap and uncertainty report; and mandates working in eight controlled 25-step supervisory batches, after each of which results must be persisted, traceability updated, new contradictions and unresolved predecessor questions identified, implications for the final theory drawn, the dependency graph updated, and work stopped for a checkpoint if a load-bearing contradiction is revealed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 1 — Semantic / theoretical validity ... Level 2 — Computational validity ... Level 3 — Efficiency and accuracy ... Level 4 — Architectural realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a strict four-level verification ordering for the KnowledgeOS theory: Level 1 asks whether the theory is a coherent, consistent mathematical model (possible verdicts VALID/CONDITIONALLY VALID/INCONSISTENT/UNDER-SPECIFIED/OPEN); Level 2 asks whether it can actually be computed (given F in K_{t+1}=F(K_t,E_t,A_t), Level 1 asks if F is well-defined, Level 2 asks if F can be computed); Level 3 asks whether it can be made more efficient/accurate WITHOUT changing its semantics ('optimization must not change the semantics of the theory... otherwise we haven't optimized the theory, we've created a different theory'); Level 4 asks whether the architecture correctly implements the verified theory. Each level presupposes the previous one survives first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CURRENT KNOWLEDGEOS CORPUS -> Candidate Theory (M0) -> VERIFY SESSION (Level 1 Math/Stats, Level 2 Computability, Level 3 Optimization, Level 4 Architecture) -> Findings/Proofs/Counterexamples/Gaps -> Human disposition -> Revised Theory -> Independent verification -> VERIFIED KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY
b_rows_sample.statement: States the overall strategic pipeline: only a Revised Theory that has passed the full Level 1-4 verify cycle AND an independent re-verification deserves the label 'Verified KnowledgeOS Theory' -- the final theory is explicitly an outcome of verification, never an assumption made at the book's outset.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Edition 2 records the best evidence-supported reconstruction of KnowledgeOS. Theory Verification determines whether that reconstruction is mathematically valid. Optimization determines whether it can be made computationally efficient and statistically accurate. Architecture determines whether the ve
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governing principle intended for the whole programme, cleanly separating four distinct questions (best-evidence reconstruction / mathematical validity / computational-statistical efficiency / faithful architectural realization) into four distinct activities, none of which should be conflated with another.

b_rows_sample.anchor: You MUST simultaneously act as: 1. Senior Mathematician ... 2. Senior Statistician ... 3. Senior DDD / Enterprise Architect ... 4. Senior Knowledge Engineer
b_rows_sample.statement: The session assigns the reviewer four simultaneous roles (mathematician, statistician, DDD/enterprise architect, knowledge engineer) and states the reviewer is 'an independent theory researcher', not a document editor.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: '200-step-longitudinal-verification-programme' POSSIBLY relates to 'theory-verification-programme-four-levels' (batch B0036). Note: A master session prompt (S1474, 2026-08-29 1606) launching a document-by-document, chronological reconstruction and verification of the entire phase_measure_theory corpus (~200 numbered steps), distinct from (but plausibly a sub-programme of) the four-level Theory Verification Programme: it centers on QUESTION->LATER-ANSWER chains, LOST_IN_EVOLUTION detection, backward/forward traceability, and independently reconstructing the final theory from the corpus rather than editing the existing final document. Defines its own epistemic-role vocabulary (14 categories), derivation verdicts (5), computability verdicts (5), evolution-status vocabulary (8, including LOST_IN_EVOLUTION), test-evidence distinctions (4), and a 17-item final status vocabulary -- all distinct enumerations from the T0-T6 ladder and 14-item theory-gap taxonomy introduced by the four-level programme's own master prompt (S1432, B0035).

a_rows_sample.anchor: p-hacking, optional stopping, publication bias, HARKing, novelty bias, selective reporting, repeated testing, slicing data until something 'significant' appears. ... Evidence acquisition provenance must include the analytical path.
a_rows_sample.statement: Replication-crisis anti-pattern (Wansink subgroup-slicing example) extends evidence provenance from Source+Acquisition to also include Selection/Transformation/Analysis/Exclusion/Publication provenance, formalized as AnalyticalLineage (Raw Dataset->Cleaning->Exclusions->Transformation->Subgroup selection->Statistical test->Model->Result->Claim) reconstructible by KnowledgeOS, protecting against a result appearing only after twenty undocumented analytical decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A replication should not merely overwrite the original result. It becomes new evidence about the original claim. ... EvidenceEpisode: original acquisition, replication, contradiction, extension, failed replication, synthesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: EvidenceEpisode object accumulates a claim's evidence history (original acquisition, replication, contradiction, extension, failed replication, synthesis) rather than letting a replication silently overwrite the original result, grounded in the Reproducibility Project's warning against treating an initial significant result as sufficient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Daoist thinking is uncomfortable with the idea that reality consists of isolated objects possessing fixed meanings independently of their relationships and circumstances. ... E = 95% of deployments succeeded ... Relative to what?
b_rows_sample.statement: Chinese/Daoist relational lens: a bare statistic ('95% of deployments succeeded') is meaningless without its relations (which deployments/teams/systems/period/procedure/risk class/exclusions/environment/what changed); its relations are part of its meaning, motivating Situational Provenance as a third provenance axis alongside Source and Method.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REALITY -> occurs -> PHENOMENON -> encounter/detection -> OBSERVATION -> acquisition context -> OBSERVATION RECORD -> assessment -> CANDIDATE EVIDENCE -> relation to hypothesis -> EVIDENCE -> synthesis -> KNOWLEDGE -> judgement -> WISDOM -> ACTION ... plus SITUATION{PERSON/TIME/RELATION -> ROLE/CHANGE/CONTEXT} feeding OBSERVATION.
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines the Zero-Lens occurrence-to-action chain with the Chinese relational structure, concluding 'the observation is never epistemically naked' -- every observation is fed by Situation{Person/Role, Time/Change, Relation/Context}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence is not a thing that KnowledgeOS merely stores. Evidence is a status that an observation may acquire through a defensible relationship between phenomenon, observation, acquisition procedure, situation, hypothesis and explanation. ... An observation cannot be fully understood apart from the situation, relationships, conditions and transformations through which it arose.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two culminating principles: evidence is a status an observation may acquire through a defensible relationship among phenomenon/observation/acquisition procedure/situation/hypothesis/explanation (substantially stronger than 'evidence has provenance'); and an observation cannot be fully understood apart from the situation/relationships/conditions/transformations through which it arose -- so the epistemic object is Evidence + arising conditions + acquisition path + relational context + transformation history.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'analytical-lineage-object' POSSIBLY relates to 'situational-provenance' (batch B0012). Note: Extends the source+acquisition provenance model with Selection/Transformation/Analysis/Exclusion/Publication provenance, motivated by the replication-crisis anti-pattern (p-hacking, optional stopping, HARKing, subgroup slicing); proposes AnalyticalLineage (Raw Dataset->Cleaning->Exclusions->Transformation->Subgroup selection->Statistical test->Model->Result->Claim) and EvidenceEpisode (original acquisition/replication/contradiction/extension/failed replication/synthesis) so a claim accumulates a reconstructible evidence history rather than a single overwritten result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ownership table — headers read, not inferred
a_rows_sample.statement: A table maps each of five viewpoints (Semantic, Structural, Behavioral, Governance-hypothesis, Operational) to its carrying asset(s), its owner read verbatim from the asset's header (e.g. 'Owner: Decision Authority', 'owner: nab.raj.sharma'), and its ladder status (executable/CANDIDATE, DRAFT, operating).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Finding 1 — ownership does NOT cut along viewpoint lines
a_rows_sample.statement: Running the reviewer's own test ('ownership signals bounded contexts') against the ownership table returns a verdict against viewpoints-as-contexts: every governed platform-side viewpoint asset resolves to the same owner, the Decision Authority (semantic-governed -> the space owner; structural -> DA twice; behavioral -> DA twice; governance -> DA; operational -> DP-bound capabilities under DA's catalog).

a_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 (review 2026-08-03): the inference was TOO STRONG — ownership is evidence, not proof
a_rows_sample.statement: The original one-owner-implies-one-context inference is downgraded: a single Chief Architect may legitimately own three genuine bounded contexts, so shared ownership is evidence against separate bounded contexts but insufficient by itself to establish a single one. The weaker claim still carries the conclusion jointly with the language test (no viewpoint has its own ubiquitous language) and the ARB's 'complementary siblings' line: viewpoints are not bounded contexts and must never be teamed, owned, or governed separately.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The answer map — every commissioned question → its existing answer
a_rows_sample.statement: A table maps eleven commissioned questions (mission, vision, domains, bounded contexts, core/supporting/generic, context map, lifecycle, knowledge flow, capability model, runtime boundary, PKS boundary, product boundary) to where each is already answered in the frozen corpus, with a grade (Confirmed/Candidate/Hypothesis/Open Question), whether it was blind-validated, and the gate door it routes to.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context Map — one evidenced edge (the product BINDS the platform) + boundaries + the knowledge-flow/authority-flow inversion
a_rows_sample.statement: The context map records one evidenced edge (the product binds the platform) plus boundaries and a knowledge-flow/authority-flow inversion, but is deliberately incomplete: Evans/Vernon relationship patterns are withheld under a standing ARB ruling that 'the relationship is the conclusion'. D-3 blocks the map section of Phase C.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R-2 | Upstream/downstream assignments per context ... constrained, not missing
a_rows_sample.statement: R-2: upstream/downstream assignments per context are constrained rather than missing — a standing ARB ruling defers pattern assignment until evidence; one edge is already evidenced.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R-4 | Whether the platform's own frozen BC-1..BC-6 map and PD-1..PD-6 reconcile ... already queued as D-3
a_rows_sample.statement: R-4: whether the platform's own frozen BC-1..BC-6 bounded-context map and PD-1..PD-6 platform-domain map reconcile is already queued as D-3; this commission adds urgency, not novelty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R-8 | Product —binds→ Platform (Product Primacy as a direction of service) | HIGH
a_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-8: Product binds Platform (Product Primacy as direction of service). External support: Team Topologies — platform teams exist to serve stream-aligned teams; the product team is the platform's customer; the direction matches AIP-14 exactly. No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge | Evidence | Governance(Decision+Authority+Policy) | Assurance(Verification+Finding) | Engineering State(Observation+Action)
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists five candidate KnowledgeOS bounded contexts (Knowledge; Evidence; Governance=Decision+Authority+Policy; Assurance=Verification+Finding; Engineering State=Observation+Action), explicitly as conceptual candidates, not confirmed bounded contexts, warning ConceptualGrouping ≠ ConfirmedBoundedContext — validation must check ownership, language, lifecycle, invariants, transactions, and organizational boundaries.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Which of these concepts actually form coherent bounded contexts with their own language, ownership, invariants, lifecycle, and consistency boundaries?
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 127 (KnowledgeOS Domain/Bounded-Context Test): brings DDD criteria back to test the five information-model candidates (Knowledge | Evidence | Governance | Assurance | Engineering State) against a three-way classification Confirmed | Candidate | Supporting Concept before letting the KnowledgeOS domain architecture become implementation structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AuthoritativeKnowledge → Provenance; CurrentKnowledge → Validity; Inference ≠ Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Knowledge as BC candidate 1: strong semantics (knowledge object, claim, source, provenance, validity, version, supersession, authoritative/inferred state), strong invariants (AuthoritativeKnowledge->Provenance, CurrentKnowledge->Validity, Inference≠Authority), a lifecycle Observed->Imported->Proposed->Verified->Approved->Authoritative->Superseded, but an unresolved ownership question — since ArchitectureKnowledge and OperationalKnowledge may have different owners, 'Knowledge' may be a domain concept rather than one BC; verdict: Strong Candidate, ConfirmedBC=NotYetEstablished.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence → Provenance; Evidence → Producer; Verification → Evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Evidence as BC candidate 2: strong identity (answers 'what supports this claim'), invariants (Evidence->Provenance, Evidence->Producer, Verification->Evidence; historical evidence must not silently disappear), lifecycle Generated->Captured->Validated->Associated->Retained->Superseded/Expired; notes Evidence is consumed by nearly everything (Knowledge/Governance/Assurance/Agents) but high consumption does not itself imply a separate BC — whether it owns an independent consistency boundary remains open; verdict: Strong Candidate, ConfirmedBC=Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision → Authority; Authority → Scope; Decision → Validity; Exception → Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Governance as BC candidate 3: very strong DDD characteristics — distinct language (policy, authority, decision, approval, delegation, exception, escalation, effective date, supersession), strong invariants, a coherent lifecycle Request->Assessment->Review->Decision->Approval->Effective->Superseded, and likely organizational ownership (GovernanceAuthority belongs to defined roles/bodies) — stronger evidence than mere tables; verdict: Very Strong BC Candidate, potentially Confirmed once ownership/implementation boundaries verified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verification → Rule; Verification → Evidence; DeterministicCheck → ReproducibleResult.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Assurance as BC candidate 4: own language (rule, check, verifier, test, result, evidence, conformance, violation, verification), purpose DetermineConformance, lifecycle Rule->Check->Execution->Result->Evidence->Finding->Verification (noting Finding could belong to Assurance or Governance depending on ownership); distinguishes Assurance ≠ Governance via example 'dependency violates architecture rule' — Assurance determines Violation=True, Governance determines what to do about it; verdict: Strong BC Candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EngineeringState = Supporting Domain, not necessarily BC
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Engineering State (candidate 5: runtime/deployment/implementation state/infrastructure/observations/actions) as problematic because it belongs to many external systems (Git, Kubernetes, Nexus, CI/CD, Monitoring) — KnowledgeOS likely consumes rather than owns it, potentially owning only ObservationRecord/EvidenceReference; verdict: Supporting Domain, not necessarily BC, explicitly to prevent KnowledgeOS becoming an accidental replacement for Git/Kubernetes/monitoring.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentInteraction = Supporting Context
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Agent Interaction (candidate 6: agent, session, task, tool, recommendation, execution, delegation) asking whether this is KnowledgeOS domain semantics or AI infrastructure; concludes AgentIdentity may belong to KnowledgeOS-facing integration while PromptManagement belongs to the agent harness; verdict: Supporting Context, not a core KnowledgeOS bounded context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy = What must/should happen; Decision = What was decided in a particular case.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Policy (candidate 7: rules, constraints, applicability, scope, exceptions, effective dates) distinguishing Policy (what must/should happen) from Decision (what was decided in a particular case), Policy->DecisionContext, leaving open whether Policy deserves its own BC independent of GovernanceDecision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → AuthorizationService.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Authorization (candidate 8: actor, resource, action, scope, delegation, permission, decision) as a classic identity/security domain likely belonging to enterprise IAM rather than KnowledgeOS; states the anti-pattern warning that KnowledgeOS should not recreate EnterpriseIAM, but consume an AuthorizationService instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Concept | Initial classification |
b_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates the eight candidates' initial classification: Knowledge/Evidence/Assurance = Strong BC candidate; Governance = Very strong BC candidate; Engineering State/Agent Interaction = Supporting/external context; Policy = Candidate, boundary unresolved; Authorization = Likely external/supporting context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance: Assess/Approve/Reject/Delegate/GrantException/Supersede. Assurance: Check/Verify/Compare/Detect/Classify. Evidence: Capture/Register/Validate/Link/Retain. Knowledge: Propose/Promote/Supersede/Invalidate/Publish/Resolve.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A2 is the one that could fail. Any future operation reading insertion order — "the first assertion wins", "the most recently added is authoritative" — breaks congruence immediately. That is a design constraint the theory now states explicitly rather than assumes silently.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit forward-looking design constraint: assumption A2 (no operation consults insertion order) is violable by future design — any future operation implementing 'first assertion wins' or 'most recently added is authoritative' semantics would break congruence immediately; the theory now states this as an explicit constraint rather than a silent assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS. Not sufficient unqualified: the assumptions are real and A2 is violable by future design. Not insufficient: no counterexample exists and none can, given A1. Not unknown: the test was constructed correctly and executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final classification: the Knowledge-State/History sufficiency question is SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS — deliberately neither 'sufficient unqualified' (the assumptions A1/A2 are real and A2 is violable), nor 'insufficient' (no counterexample exists, and none can given A1), nor 'unknown' (the test was validly constructed and executed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K answers what is known. History answers how it came to be known and by whom. Neither reduces to the other, and T needs only the first.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governing principle stated as the resolution of the state/history boundary the programme has circled since the executed History(K)!=K counterexample: K answers what is known; History answers how it came to be known and by whom; neither reduces to the other, and the transformation function T needs only K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematical existence ... Mathematical computability ... Software implementation ... Empirical validation ... These are not equivalent. Mathematically defined ⇏ implemented. Implemented ⇏ semantically equivalent. Implemented ⇏ empirically validated.
b_rows_sample.statement: A four-way separation is made mandatory: mathematical existence, mathematical computability, software implementation (code realizing the operation), and empirical validation (an executed test showing the implementation approximates the function) are all logically independent — being mathematically defined does not imply implemented, being implemented does not imply semantically equivalent, and being implemented does not imply empirically validated.

b_rows_sample.statement: The overall implementation gap is asymmetric, not total: the theory's three central objects (Assertion, K, Assessment) are all missing implementation, while adjacent mechanisms (History, Lineage, Identity, plus Evidence/Provenance/Governance infrastructure) have real, partly tested evidence — meaning KnowledgeOS implements PARTS of the conceptual machinery without yet exposing a demonstrated one-to-one realization of the canonical theoretical model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain Model ≠ Infrastructure Representation. b_rows_sample.statement: Three related DDD/methodological principles govern the whole bridge: Domain Model must not be conflated with Infrastructure Representation (an implementation can contain all the ingredients yet lack the canonical aggregate structure); correspondence must be judged by semantic equivalence, never mere class-name equivalence (K need not literally have a KnowledgeState class); and the bridge is bidirectional but asymmetric (theory dictates required semantics, implementation supplies evidence of realization) — neither side may silently redefine the other, so an implementation object (GovernanceLineageGraph) must never be equated with a theory object (K) without proof, and vice versa.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 267 final verdict: EMPIRICAL BRIDGE PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED, NOT CLOSED — History, Lineage, Identity, Evidence, Provenance infrastructure, and Authority/Governance infrastructure are strongly supported with varying test evidence; Assertion, K, and Assessment are explicit implementation gaps; the most important empirical gap is that 0 of 12 designed falsification scenarios are runnable against the real system; the theory has reached a point where empirical testing is justified, but cannot yet claim the canonical theory is implemented by the actual system.

This holds under exactly two assumptions: A1 (T reads only K, Policy, Authority — PROVEN by elimination of actor/time/evidence/context during signature derivation) and A2 (no operation consults order-of-arrival — HOLDS for the twelve derived operations because A and R are sets, making order structurally unobservable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A2 is the one that could fail. Any future operation reading insertion order — "the first assertion wins", "the most recently added is authoritative" — breaks congruence immediately. That is a design constraint the theory now states explicitly rather than assumes silently.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit forward-looking design constraint: assumption A2 (no operation consults insertion order) is violable by future design — any future operation implementing 'first assertion wins' or 'most recently added is authoritative' semantics would break congruence immediately; the theory now states this as an explicit constraint rather than a silent assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS. Not sufficient unqualified: the assumptions are real and A2 is violable by future design. Not insufficient: no counterexample exists and none can, given A1. Not unknown: the test was constructed correctly and executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final classification: the Knowledge-State/History sufficiency question is SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS — deliberately neither 'sufficient unqualified' (the assumptions A1/A2 are real and A2 is violable), nor 'insufficient' (no counterexample exists, and none can given A1), nor 'unknown' (the test was validly constructed and executed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is sufficient for FUTURE COMPUTATION. It is NOT sufficient for GOVERNANCE AUDIT. ... Who asserted this, and when? NO ... Was every admission properly authorised? NO — GovernanceValid(K,Γ) needs History ... What did we believe last March? NO — needs History
a_rows_sample.statement: The state/history sufficiency boundary is drawn precisely: K alone answers what is currently held, what follows from an operation (congruence), whether structural/semantic invariants hold, and current epistemic status (recomputable from e); K alone CANNOT answer who asserted something and when, whether every admission was properly authorised (GovernanceValid(K,Gamma) needs History), or what was believed at a past point in time (needs History or a bitemporal interpretation of t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K answers what is known. History answers how it came to be known and by whom. Neither reduces to the other, and T needs only the first.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governing principle stated as the resolution of the state/history boundary the programme has circled since the executed History(K)!=K counterexample: K answers what is known; History answers how it came to be known and by whom; neither reduces to the other, and the transformation function T needs only K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer proposes a "Provenance Domain" ... Verdict: PROVENANCE is not a missing domain — it is a DISPERSED, NAMED, PARTLY-GOVERNED concern
b_rows_sample.statement: A check-before-recording pass finds provenance already lives in the corpus as: one axis of AUTHORITY itself (provenance x standing, Engineering Progression Model, PM-1), the PROVENANCE non-progression kind, identity discipline (CAP-001), evidence grading practice ([FETCHED]/[CANONICAL]/[2nd-hand]), and append-only evidence/traceability blocks. Verdict: provenance is a dispersed, named, partly-governed concern (the SP-5 pattern recognized a third time), not a missing domain. Disposition: the provenance questions enrich the existing Tier-1 Knowledge Governance stream (PM-1); 'Provenance as a strategic domain' is recorded as a hypothesis routed to the docket, admissible only if a live stream produces evidence requiring it; the identity-chain observation (CAP-001 as foundation if provenance grows) is a watch item, not a promotion.

b_rows_sample.statement: U-GR-2: whether provenance remains an enrichment of Knowledge Governance or eventually becomes its own domain, waiting on operational evidence from the live streams, not literature.

b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1 (provenance x standing) is enriched: industry treats provenance as a governance control plane (identity -> version -> retrieval event -> evidence -> answer -> audit), paralleling P4 and resting on identity discipline (CAP-001). Provenance already lives dispersed in the corpus (authority axis, non-progression kind, evidence grading, traceability blocks); 'Provenance as its own domain' is a hypothesis at the docket, not a new backlog stream — this row owns the questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: authority = provenance × standing ... [CANONICAL] W3C PROV: derivation is an immutable provenance fact
b_rows_sample.statement: The formula authority = provenance x standing is supported by W3C PROV (derivation is an immutable provenance fact) and data-catalog practice (lineage != 'certified' flag are two independent fields in every major catalog). No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SC-5 | authority = provenance × standing in ONE field (its own header asks two questions)
b_rows_sample.statement: SC-5: authority combines provenance and standing into one field, though its own header asks two separate questions; open, routed to PM-1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL — AND IT IS MY FOURTH INSTANCE OF LEVEL CONFUSION ... I-4 is NOT falsified. I misdiagnosed a LIFECYCLE gap as an ONTOLOGY falsification
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior claim that I-4 was falsified is retracted: a discharge summary is not authoritative because it was projected, but became authoritative through DERIVED -> REVIEWED -> ATTESTED -> RELEASED; governance created the authority, not the derivation. The corrected conclusion is not 'DP-2 is wrong' but 'DP-2 conflates DERIVATION with ATTESTATION'. Four prior level confusions listed: flat vs dimensional (taxonomy), artifact vs concept (existence), layer vs sibling (ontology), lifecycle vs structure (this one). A fifth was avoided by checking: the author was about to report 'there is no lifecycle', when in fact nine exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The precise gap — located mechanically ... THE GAP: STATUS HAS A GOVERNED STATE MACHINE. AUTHORITY DOES NOT
b_rows_sample.statement: statuses.yaml and authorities.yaml are declared orthogonal but are not equally equipped: statuses.yaml has 8 values, a progression field (order), a terminal marker (settled), a defined who-may-move role table, and lint-checkable transition guards; authorities.yaml has 5 values and none of these. Authority gates a status transition, but nothing governs how authority itself changes — no rule for who may move derived->authoritative, and no guard for it. This is exactly the I-4 problem: attestation is an authority transition (derived->authoritative); because authority transitions are ungoverned, the model cannot express 'attested', so it collapses derived into 'never authoritative'. A prior reviewer's diagnosis ('DP-2 conflates derivation and attestation') now has a mechanical cause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 (WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 — ILL-POSED) ... authority is TWO dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE × act-changed STANDING
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') is withdrawn as ill-posed: the question dissolved under discovery that authority is two dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE (generated, derived) times act-changed STANDING (authoritative, provisional, historical). Provenance cannot have a state machine; standing changes by governance acts. Superseded by PM-1/PM-2, recorded in the Engineering Progression Model section 4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-2 | Restate DP-2 to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION?
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-2: should DP-2 be restated to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION — this is CV-1, now with a mechanical cause; routed to the ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Convergences — conclusions this track reached that the blind review reproduced (items 1-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve conclusions reproduced blind, now carrying double independent derivation: (1) KnowledgeOS is a hypothesis, gate shut, Vision unapproved; (2) 'PublicDigit is the laboratory' rejected against ADR-AIP-02, Product Primacy governs; (3) the EKP is a real governed context with named individual owner; (4) Engineering Governance is the strongest bounded context; (5) the reusable kernel list, near-identical; (6) designed-for-reuse != demonstrated-reusable (verbatim convergence); (7) individual EKP ownership is a succession risk, sharpened to 'separation of duties is real as process and unevidenced as people'; (8) three knowledge ontologies coexist unreconciled; (9) domain-free methodology sits in product paths, placement breached, plus a new instance (Platform_Capability_Pattern); (10) PMR-10's manual adoption failed, sharpened into a falsification of the Reference Architecture's protocol-suffices stance; (11) most of the 11 invariants reproduced with citations, with I-8 downgraded to invariant-in-waiting; (12) the split verdict itself (enacted internal mission vs unratified product vision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TWO CONCESSIONS BEFORE THE MODEL ... INTENDED is WITHDRAWN as a fourth evidence grade ... Intent is not evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior 'INTENDED' evidence grade is withdrawn: intent is not evidence, and applying the repository's own rule (determine whether a proposal is a new dimension, an overloaded existing dimension, or merely another value) shows INTENDED was an overloaded existing dimension, added inside a document about evidence discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four concerns, separated as required ... A fifth concern the repository already separates ... TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml
b_rows_sample.statement: Four concerns mapped to dimensions: EVIDENCE (D-V, new), GOVERNANCE (D-III, existing/executable via statuses.yaml), OPERATIONAL STATE (D-VI, new), INTENT (derived: f(GOVERNANCE-STATUS, OWNER), both fields already exist). A fifth concern the repository already separates, worth naming so it is not re-added later: TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml (authoritative, derived, generated, historical, provisional), and statuses.yaml already declares status independent of authority — the repository was doing orthogonal dimensions before this commission asked for them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 was solution design, conceded ... exactly what DDD forbids. I located an asymmetry and immediately proposed its repair
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('missing transitions -> need a state machine') is conceded as solution design: an inference from a missing implementation to a model, which DDD forbids — an asymmetry was located and its repair immediately proposed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer's "that chain is QUALIFICATION, not authority" — CONFIRMED by the repository ... DERIVED → REVIEWED → ATTESTED → RELEASED describes a document becoming more trustworthy
b_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's claim that the DERIVED->REVIEWED->ATTESTED->RELEASED chain describes qualification, not authority, is confirmed: the repository already has vocabulary for it (ES-006.1's qualification stage, ES-003 Qualification), though 'Qualification' also carries a recorded UL collision (verification activity vs promotion-ladder stage), now with a third candidate sense (the standing-assignment chain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The progression mechanisms — inventoried as evidence (P-1..P-10)
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten progression mechanisms inventoried as observations, not assumed lifecycles: P-1 document status (8 values, order+settled+roles+guards); P-2 Authority (5 values with rank, no order/roles/guards); P-3 ES-006.1 promotion ladder; P-4 Methodology maturity; P-5 ADR-M status; P-6 Capability lifecycle; P-7 EEP (plan->...->decide); P-8 Observation Protocol (ACTIVE->CONCLUDED); P-9 Identifier lifecycles (4 series); P-10 Evidence accumulation (n=0->n=1->n>=2). A prior canonical distinction (Reference Model section 6, GEP-F1: two lifecycles never conflated, governance-artifact vs governed-work) is found before theorizing; this discovery extends that refusal rather than founding it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The flagship finding — authority is not one dimension ... authorities.yaml's own header asks TWO questions in ONE field: "how much should I trust this and where did it come from?"
b_rows_sample.statement: authorities.yaml's five values answer two different questions: 'generated' and 'derived' answer provenance (where did it come from), and can never change (origin is an immutable historical fact); 'authoritative', 'provisional', and 'historical' answer standing (how much should I trust it), and can change by a governance act. This dissolves LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') rather than answering it: half of authority cannot have a state machine (provenance never changes) and the other half changes by governance acts recorded as act-logs, not workflows. Authority = an immutable PROVENANCE fact x a mutable STANDING judgment; attestation changes standing, nothing changes provenance. This also explains why the I-4 confusion was persistent: 'derived' (provenance) was wrongly read as entailing low standing, but a signed financial statement can be derived in provenance and authoritative in standing simultaneously.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 | Should authority's two questions — provenance and standing — be separated?
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1: should authority's two questions, provenance and standing, be separated — this supersedes LG-1, which is withdrawn as ill-posed — authority: ARB + PD-3's owner.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-2 | Should standing-changes (attestation, supersession) get the role/guard treatment status-changes have?
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-2: should standing-changes get the role/guard treatment status-changes have — an act-governance question, not a state-machine question — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant relationships vs implementation choices ... I-1..I-11 ... 11 invariants · 8 choices
b_rows_sample.statement: Eleven invariants traced to governed statements: I-1 Knowledge is represented by an Artifact, an Artifact is never the Knowledge; I-2 a Capability protects exactly one invariant; I-3 a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary; I-4 (underspecified, not false — holds until attestation, reclassified as a lifecycle gap not an ontology falsification, per DP-2's conflation of derivation with attestation); I-5 one authoritative artifact per topic+context (lint-enforced); I-6 the Runtime never owns Knowledge; I-7 a PKS never contains reusable Method (stated and breached); I-8 governance precedes automation; I-9 governance-status orthogonal to authority; I-10 a constitutional principle is void-overriding; I-11 (restated 2026-08-02: Knowledge does not execute, capabilities execute, knowledge constrains and informs generation — the restatement survived cross-product projection where the original would have failed). Eight implementation choices (folder mapping, markdown as representation, YAML/Mermaid, the graph's declared scope, Claude Code as the n=1 runtime adapter, frontmatter, identifier formats, Mermaid+markdown projections) may change freely without breaking the model — that distinction is what makes this a platform rather than a repository layout.

a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.

a_rows_sample.statement: Original (later superseded) analysis: mapping the nine-stage policy-to-effect path (definition, derivation, evaluation, observation, admission control, blocking/halt, escalation, audit, advisory tripwires) against evidence shows every stage already performed by an owned capability (chiefly CAP-09/BC-3), so EKS-02's gap is a coverage gap within existing machinery, not a missing capability -- this categorical denial is itself withdrawn later by Amendment 1 as a category argument doing an existence test's job.

a_rows_sample.statement: C-14's categorical denial is replaced by provisional wording: no platform-wide C-14 capability is established, but a Tier-1 enforcement pattern exists within CAP-09, and whether that instance is the same capability as C-14 is OQ-H, unresolved -- with four separated sub-concerns (policy tier assignment, coverage mapping, enforcement execution, enforcement assurance), each with a different owner status.

a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a prior claim that C-14 policy-enforcement is 'absent': one asset (AST-007) is mechanically blocking and in production, so the correct classification is a coverage gap for the narrower C-15 claim, not an absent capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \forall F\in\mathcal F_{\text{core}}, \quad F\text{ is formally defined} \land F\text{ is computable} \land F\text{ has an observable input}
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the Computational Realizability Principle as a new verification phase: for every core primitive operation, it must be formally defined, computable, and have an observable input. Computable ≠ Perfect — KnowledgeOS does not need perfect observation/parsing/inference, only the ability to represent what it observed, how, how reliably, and what remains unknown. Formal statement: ∀f∈F_core there exist an observable input space X_f, an output space Y_f, and f:X_f->Y_f implementable by a finite computational procedure, possibly with explicitly represented uncertainty or nondeterminism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticParse \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks 14 core primitives (Receive Intent, Structural Parse, Semantic Reconstruction, Dimension Discovery, Acquire Evidence, Create Observation, Create Assertion, Coherence Checking, Conflict Detection, Gap Detection, Discrepancy, Distance, Sārathi Navigation, Lord) through a computability check, each judged computable but with varying determinism. Notably SemanticParse->CandidateMeaning, not SemanticParse->Truth (semantic parsing is probabilistic, not a deterministic oracle), and Candidate ≠ Knowledge for Lord's outputs. Coherence/Conflict/Gap detection are judged deterministic PROVIDED the relevant rules/Ideal-State are made explicit (e.g. conflict example: two Nexus-version assertions on the same entity/dimension/context/validity interval trigger a deterministic 'potential contradiction' flag, without the system knowing which is true).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Deterministic

Schema validation
Type checking
a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies KnowledgeOS operations into four categories: Deterministic (schema validation, type checking, set/temporal comparison, conflict rule evaluation, gap calculation, hashing, provenance linkage); Probabilistic (language interpretation, semantic reconstruction, entity resolution, classification, candidate generation, inference); Policy-dependent (severity, adequacy, ideal-state selection, prioritization, resolution strategy); Human-authoritative (decisions intentionally requiring human approval — 'not a failure of KnowledgeOS, a governance boundary'). Also shows an LLM can participate in KnowledgeOS (as Parser/LLM/Database feeding Evidence->Observation->Knowledge) without becoming KnowledgeOS: the LLM performs semantic interpretation/candidate/hypothesis generation/summarization/reasoning assistance, while KnowledgeOS retains control of identity, provenance, evidence, state, epistemic status, coherence, conflicts, gaps, transitions, governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question 19A — Computational Realizability of KnowledgeOS
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical expansion (before Questions 20+) to insert Question 19A — Computational Realizability of KnowledgeOS: for every primitive, answer (1) what is the input, (2) can it be observed/acquired, (3) what algorithm/process computes it, (4) what is the output, (5) deterministic/probabilistic/policy-dependent?, (6) what uncertainty is preserved, (7) what evidence/provenance is attached, (8) what happens on computation failure, (9) can the result be reproduced, (10) can another KnowledgeOS instance verify it. Answering these for every primitive would give 'the beginnings of an executable mathematical specification for KnowledgeOS' — proposed as the correct next milestone before 'closing the theory'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation = Acquired\ information\ through\ a\ defined\ observation\ channel
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the earlier worry that Observation might not be computable: Observation is not restricted to sensors — it can come from a database query, document extraction, web retrieval, a human statement, or a runtime API result, each shown as a channel->artifact->Observation pipeline. Formalizes Observe:(Source,AcquisitionMethod,Artifact,Context,Time)->Observation, implementable via ordinary technology (parsers, DB drivers, HTTP clients, APIs, filesystem/Git access, OCR, speech-to-text, structured parsers, LLMs, rule engines, human input interfaces) — 'Observation is computationally realizable.'
