a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies theory maturity into three levels: L1 Conceptual definition (know what a thing means, mostly resolved), L2 Mathematical specification (can define inputs/outputs/invariants, mostly resolved), L3 Computable semantics (know an executable algorithm producing the result, NOT completely resolved) — the theory has reached L2 for most of the architecture but not L3 everywhere.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observe ... Interpret ... DiscoverDimensions ... AssessEvidence ... DetectConflict ... EvaluateCoherence ... ConstructIdeal ... MeasureDiscrepancy
a_rows_sample.statement: Names eight operators still requiring computational closure, each individually diagnosed: Observe(x,C) (what makes a database row / human statement / LLM output / sensor reading count as an observation, still unformalized); semantic reconstruction f_semantic:Text×Context->SemanticRepresentation (unspecified, needed to detect when a question is insufficiently specified and generate clarification); DiscoverDimensions (needs an acceptance criterion for when a candidate dimension is sufficiently justified to enter the Knowledge Model); AssessEvidence(E,A,C)->(Support,Uncertainty,Validity) (needs to account for source reliability, relevance, independence, corroboration, contradiction, temporal validity, provenance, having rejected Support=Probability); DetectConflict (ConflictDetection=RuleEvaluation, needing SameSubject∧SameDimension∧CompatibleScope∧TemporalOverlap∧IncompatibleValues, with the rule language/semantics unspecified); EvaluateCoherence (Coherent(K)=W∧L∧E∧T∧C is defined but each predicate like Logical(K) or Contextual(K) still needs an executable validator); ConstructIdeal (needs an Ideal-State authority model — who determines what is desired: Human/Constitution/Policy/Domain rules/Purpose/Manifesto/ADR/System configuration/LLM proposal/Negotiation — otherwise KnowledgeOS could manufacture an unauthorized 'ideal'); MeasureDiscrepancy (Δ≠necessarily one scalar is settled, but numeric d(x,y)=|x-y| vs categorical d(Confirmed,Observed) vs understanding-distance d(U_1,U_2) may not even be a metric, favoring 'Typed Discrepancy' over one universal distance function).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deterministic\ Kernel + Explicit\ Policy + Probabilistic/AI\ Proposals + Human\ Authority
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three computational classes: Class A Deterministic (schema, types, relations, temporal/logical rules, provenance, state transitions, constraint checking, hashing, identity — machine-verifiable); Class B Policy-governed (evidence sufficiency, severity, relevance, ideal-state requirements, conflict policies, acceptance thresholds — explicit policies, not mathematical truths); Class C Generative/interpretive (semantic parsing, dimension discovery, hypothesis/question generation, interpretation, horizon expansion — AI/LLM output enters as Candidate, never automatically as Truth). Resulting architecture: Deterministic Kernel + Explicit Policy + Probabilistic/AI Proposals + Human Authority, rather than pretending everything is mathematically objective.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every unresolved computation has an identifiable boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: not 'the complete mathematical model is finished' but 'the conceptual and structural mathematical model is substantially complete, but the operational semantics of several epistemic operators remain to be formally specified' — none of the eight named operators is an 'undefined philosophical black hole' any more; every unresolved computation has an identifiable boundary. Recommends a 'KnowledgeOS Computational Closure' phase: for every operator specify Domain->Input Types->Preconditions->Algorithm->Output Type->Invariants->Failure Modes, tested against concrete examples (Arjuna/Gita, Nexus infrastructure, software architecture, ADRs, databases, internet sources, LLM outputs, human instructions), giving the chain Theory->Formal Model->Computational Model->Executable KnowledgeOS as the point at which implementation may responsibly begin.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM: Observation \rightarrow Interpretation
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows exactly where the LLM fits without bypassing the epistemic boundary: LLM:Observation->Interpretation, or LLM:Question->CandidateDimensions, or LLM:KnowledgeState->CandidateHypothesis; every LLM output flows through KnowledgeOS rules and is either Accepted or Rejected before reaching the Knowledge State — 'one of the most important architectural properties of KnowledgeOS'. Per-operator computability check: Observe (yes, via database query/HTTP response/file read/human statement/LLM response/sensor); Interpret (yes but heterogeneous — parser/ontology/rules/LLM/human interpretation, result always a candidate); Assess (yes if policies explicit); Construct Assertion (yes); Update Knowledge State (yes).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Acquisition Closure
a_rows_sample.statement: States the 'KnowledgeOS Acquisition Closure' result: every admissible information source can be transformed into a provenance-bearing artifact, observed through an explicit acquisition operation, interpreted into candidate semantic objects, epistemically assessed, and (if accepted under governing rules) incorporated into the Knowledge State — stronger than 'KnowledgeOS can read documents'. But flags Interpretation as still only architecturally, not fully computationally, closed: must handle unstructured text, incomplete questions, ambiguity, multiple possible interpretations, domain-specific meaning, implicit dimensions, contradictory interpretations, and LLM-generated interpretations — proposing 'Computational Closure 1 — Observation' then 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation and Dimension Discovery' as the next concrete steps in place of proceeding to Question 21.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ARCHITECTURALLY CLOSED, SEMANTICALLY OPEN
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares Source Observation CLOSED and Interpretation 'ARCHITECTURALLY CLOSED, SEMANTICALLY OPEN' — we know how the operation works structurally, but the interpretation content may legitimately remain ambiguous, incomplete, multiple, AI-assisted, human-assisted, or domain-dependent, which is 'not a defect'; forcing interpretation to be deterministic would damage the model. Proposes a Semantic Reconstruction bounded context owning SemanticInterpretation/CandidateDimension/CandidateEntity/CandidateRelationship/CandidateProposition/Ambiguity/InterpretationMethod/InterpretationEvidence but explicitly NOT owning truth, final epistemic status, domain authority, or governance decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Input → Artifact | Closed ... Assertion ↔ Gap | Needs gap detector formalization
a_rows_sample.statement: Nine-row closure-status table: Input->Artifact (Closed), Artifact->SourceObservation (Closed), SourceObservation->Interpretation (architecturally closed, interpretation can be ambiguous), Interpretation->CandidateProposition (Closed), CandidateProposition->Assertion (closed conceptually, admission policy remains configurable), Assertion->KnowledgeState (Closed), Assertion<->Evidence (needs formal evidence model), Assertion<->Conflict (needs conflict-rule formalization), Assertion<->Gap (needs gap-detector formalization). Names 'Evidence' as the next major closure target: what counts as evidence, how it relates to an assertion, how it can be computationally evaluated without reducing epistemic reasoning to an arbitrary confidence score, to be tested against direct measurement/DB output/document statement/human testimony/expert opinion/LLM output/derived calculation/multiple independent sources/circular sources/stale sources/contradictory sources, aiming to make Assess(A,E,Π,C)->Σ_A 'computationally realizable rather than merely philosophical'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Computability boundary: undecidability, three distinct failure modes, and the Unknown/Uncomputable/Intractable distinction
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes simple graph/temporal/provenance queries and deterministic invariant checks are cheaply computable (e.g. O(V+E), O(1)), but reachability/state-explosion can be intractable (n binary variables give |S|=2^n, e.g. 2^100 for n=100, not enumerable), mitigated by abstraction/symbolic reasoning/compositional verification (linking back to Step 48). Statistical operations (mean, variance, regression, Bayesian updating, hypothesis testing) are generally feasible; causal inference has no single complexity class (combinatorial search, latent variables, model uncertainty, missing data); decision optimization can become NP-hard. States a fundamental computability limitation: some questions about arbitrary programs (e.g. halting) are undecidable, so KnowledgeOS cannot promise UniversalVerification and must support Unknown as a legitimate final result. Strengthens Step 41's Unknown by adding Uncomputable and Intractable as distinct categories, and separates three non-conflatable failure modes: epistemic failure (InsufficientEvidence), computational failure (CannotComputeWithinBudget), and mathematical limitation (Undecidable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Computational budget, graceful degradation with mandatory status preservation, ComputeResult contract with error bounds
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Budget=(Time,Memory,Cost) and Compute(f,Budget) returning ExactResult, Approximation, or Unresolved. Requires graceful degradation Exact -> Approximate -> Heuristic -> Unknown while the system 'must preserve the status' -- explicitly forbidding silent approximation (ExactFailure -> Guess presented as fact); instead ApproximationUsed=True must be recorded. Defines a formal computational contract ComputeResult = (Value, Method, Status, ErrorBound, Cost) (example: Value=tau-hat, Method=MonteCarlo, Status=Approximate, ErrorBound=epsilon) -- 'mathematically much stronger than returning only a number' -- and requires an error bound |x-hat - x|<=epsilon be reported only when meaningful, never invented. Also classifies ReasoningMode in {Formal, Deterministic, Statistical, Probabilistic, Heuristic, LLMGenerated}, each with different assurance characteristics; an LLM-generated conclusion is CandidateInference, not automatically equivalent to FormalInference -- 'this preserves our epistemic firewall'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 49 primitive-reduction model (all PASS)
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) can Evidence exist without Observation? No => Evidence is derived; (2) can Provenance exist without Relations? No => Provenance is relational structure; (3) can Causality be represented as generic RelatedTo? Not safely => Causes must be a typed relation; (4) can Learning be represented as a static object? Not adequately => it is a transition K_t->K_{t+1}; (5) can Decision be separated from Action? Yes => Decision->Action, preserving authorization/dry-run semantics; (6) can Outcome be treated as Decision? No => an outcome is a post-action observation; (7) can Unknown be represented as False? No => the three-valued epistemic distinction remains necessary; (8) can approximate computation be represented as exact? No => computation status must be retained; (9) can every theoretical KnowledgeOS question be computed exactly? No => undecidability/complexity impose limits; (10) does mathematical complexity require special hardware? Not necessarily => complexity determines resource requirements, not model validity; (11) can the same domain model run on local or distributed infrastructure? Yes, if ports/contracts isolate infrastructure; (12) can a new concept be added without increasing the primitive kernel? Yes, if derivable from existing primitives.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three execution classes (deterministic/statistical/AI) behind a ComputePort; no infrastructure leakage into the domain
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a statistical Result=(Estimate,Method,ModelVersion,Uncertainty,Status) type (e.g. mu-hat=12.4, CI95%=[11.7,13.1], interval preserved, no false precision beyond what the measurement supports) and reiterates Status in {Exact,Approximate,Simulation,Heuristic,Unresolved}. States the reference implementation's core computation is intentionally modest (CoreComputation << ExternalSpecializedComputation), giving DeterministicCore + PluggableCompute across three execution classes: Class A deterministic domain computation (runs locally), Class B statistical computation (local or via compute adapter), Class C AI inference (external/local model provider) -- all returning governed results through a ComputePort: Input -> ComputedResult, implementable as LocalPython/Java/RemoteService while the domain remains independent (no 'if kubernetes/postgres/openai/claude' branching inside the domain).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three-boundary hierarchy Observable→Identifiable→Computable (none reversible); refines the normal-PC question
a_rows_sample.statement: States Computable != Observable (easy to compute but impossible to observe from available data), Observable != Identifiable (observed variables may still lack enough information to identify a causal/statistical quantity), and Identifiable != ComputationallyCheap (an identified problem can still be computationally expensive) -- giving the three-boundary hierarchy Observable -> Identifiable -> Computable, none of the implications automatically reversible. States this directly refines the recurring 'runs on a normal PC' question: cheap computability does not make an answer epistemically valid, and a theoretically identifiable problem may need a cluster to compute efficiently -- hardware capacity is only one dimension. Experiment 12: two states producing identical (trivially computable) observations remain NotIdentifiable -- PASS. Experiment 13: a large but theoretically identifiable inference problem returns Identified=True with ComputationalCost=High -- PASS. Defines the resulting layered boundary Reality -Observation-> ObservableWorld -Inference-> IdentifiedKnowledge -Computation-> DecisionSupport, 'prevents category errors'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Normal-PC feasibility for core operations; example complexity (graph traversal, indexed lookup); provenance-lookup experiment
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists operations a normal modern PC can execute: GraphTraversal, SchemaValidation, TypeChecking, ProvenanceChecking, HashVerification, EventProcessing, RuleEvaluation, ModerateStatisticalAnalysis -- 'not inherently distributed'. Gives example complexity O(V+E) for graph traversal (e.g. V=1,000,000, E=5,000,000, manageable on a single machine with engineering optimization) and O(log n) or near-constant indexed lookups (e.g. find EvidenceByClaimId). Experiment 4: retrieving all direct evidence references for a claim is a Finite Query -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture != Algorithm; finite representation x∈Σ*; state transition T:S×E→S∪Error rejecting invariant violations
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS's architecture can specify semantic contracts (Knowledge, Evidence, Inference, Causality, Decision) without mandating one universal algorithm per operation -- Architecture != Algorithm, allowing multiple computational implementations. Requires every artifact to have a finite representation x in Sigma* (JSON, database records, graph nodes, event records, model metadata, hashes, identifiers). Formalizes S_{t+1}=T(S_t,e_t) as an executable event-transition chain, and strengthens T to T: S x E -> S union Error, rejecting an event when it would violate an invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiments 1-3: finite state transition, invalid-type-transition rejection, deterministic-bounds-checked probabilistic claim acceptance
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: computing T(S0,e1) yields S1 as ordinary computation -- PASS. Experiment 2: attempting Prediction->VerifiedFact with no validation evidence yields T(S,e)=EpistemicTypeError -- PASS, illustrating that deterministic rule evaluation (if type(x)=Prediction and target=VerifiedFact and not-Validated then Reject) does not require an AI to 'understand' the rule -- 'exactly where deterministic assurance becomes powerful'. Separates deterministic computation f(x)=y from probabilistic computation P(Y|X): the deterministic layer verifies schema/type/provenance/authorization/invariant-satisfaction/graph-integrity/version-compatibility/cryptographic-integrity, while the AI/statistical layer performs inference/prediction/classification/hypothesis-generation/probabilistic-reasoning -- giving 'AI reasoning + Deterministic assurance'. Experiment 3: an AI output P(p)=0.82 checked deterministically for 0<=0.82<=1 plus ModelVersion/Provenance yields AcceptedAsProbabilisticClaim -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Computability != Feasibility; deployment independence of semantic results; three computational classes
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Class A Easy/ordinary (O(n), O(n log n)), Class B Expensive but computable (O(n^2), O(n^3), or exponential for modest n), Class C Not generally computable (no general algorithm) -- 'expensive is not the same as uncomputable'. States a problem may be Computable=True yet Practically Infeasible=True (e.g. requiring 10^100 operations) -- Computability != Feasibility. Experiment 5: a finite optimization problem whose exact solution requires enormous computation is Computable but PracticallyInfeasible -- PASS. Introduces a ComputationalProfile C=(Time,Memory,DataVolume,ModelSize,Parallelism) metadata concept, classifying operations as Local/Parallel/Distributed/ExternalService (e.g. TypeCheck/ProvenanceValidation/SmallGraphTraversal/RuleEvaluation locally; LLMInference/LargeEmbeddingGeneration/LargeSimulation on GPU/large machines; MassiveDataProcessing/LargeScaleModelTraining potentially distributed). States the architectural principle SemanticArchitecture should not depend on ComputationalDeployment: the same semantic operation may run locally or distributed. Experiment 6: validating I(x) on laptop/server/distributed worker yields SameSemanticResult given deterministic implementation and equivalent inputs -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State-space explosion avoided via symbolic representation and solver delegation; KnowledgeOS should not become a UniversalSolver
b_rows_sample.statement: For n binary variables the state space is 2^n (e.g. ~1.27e30 for n=100), which cannot be enumerated -- but KnowledgeOS does not need to: it can represent CurrentState and Constraints symbolically (e.g. x1+x2<=1) and delegate to constraint solving/SAT-SMT/symbolic algebra/optimization engines. Experiment 7: attempting to enumerate 100 binary variables' full state space is ComputationallyInfeasible, but the symbolic representation remains manageable -- PASS. States the DDD conclusion: KnowledgeOS should not become a UniversalSolver; it defines the SemanticContract and delegates specialized computation. Experiment 8: KnowledgeOS creates a SolverRequest for an OptimizationProblem, receives a Solution from an external solver, and validates the result and provenance rather than implementing every optimizer internally -- PASS, giving a clean architecture (Rule Engine / Statistics / AI-ML feeding a Validated Result under KnowledgeOS governance).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Undecidability re-derived; undecidable-request refusal experiment; six-item EpistemicLimit taxonomy
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives that a universal termination check (halting problem) is not computable, and that this does not invalidate KnowledgeOS: it must instead represent Unknown or UndecidableUnderCurrentModel. Experiment 9: asked to determine termination for every arbitrary program, the system correctly returns NoUniversalAlgorithm rather than fabricating an answer -- PASS. Consolidates a formal limitation taxonomy EpistemicLimit = {Unknown, Uncertain, Unobservable, NonIdentified, Infeasible, Undecidable}, each with different meanings and remedies. Experiment 10: constructing one example of each limitation, the system preserves their distinct semantic reasons rather than collapsing them into a generic 'error' -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent workflow termination controls: cycle detection and execution budgets (MaxSteps/MaxTime/MaxTokens/MaxCost/MaxDepth)
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns an unbounded agent workflow (A->B->C->A) can loop forever, requiring termination controls. Experiment 11: A->B->A correctly yields CycleDetected or ExecutionBudgetExceeded -- PASS. Defines execution budget dimensions MaxSteps, MaxTime, MaxTokens, MaxCost, MaxDepth, making AI computation operationally controllable and runnable locally (e.g. MaxSteps=20 guarantees termination even on non-convergent reasoning). Experiment 12: an agent failing to converge after 20 iterations yields ReasoningTimeout rather than infinite execution -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sound vs Complete distinction; soundness preferred for high-integrity subsystems; finite-test-extrapolation rejected
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Sound (if the system derives p, p is valid under its rules) from Complete (if p is derivable under the rules, the system will find it) as different properties. States for high-integrity transformations FalsePositive may be more dangerous than FalseNegative, so some subsystems should prioritize Soundness. Experiment 13: a validator checking only known invariant violations (not proving no unknown issue exists) correctly yields ValidatedUnderRules rather than AbsolutelyCorrect -- PASS, giving the defensible statement 'the artifact satisfies the specified validation rules' rather than 'reality is correct'. Notes some components may be formally proved (for-all x in D: I(x)) while others can only be tested on finite examples (I(x_1),...,I(x_n)), which never establishes universal correctness. Experiment 14: 1,000 successful tests do not license an AI claiming SystemCorrectForAllInputs -- Rejected -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Five-level assurance hierarchy; assurance-inflation rejection experiment
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes a testing/verification hierarchy: ExampleTest, PropertyTest, InvariantTest, ModelCheck, FormalProof, each providing different assurance, and defines an AssuranceLevel taxonomy Observed / Tested / InvariantValidated / FormallyVerified -- 'not one universal truth score'. Experiment 15: a component passing only unit tests being labeled FormallyVerified is Rejected -- PASS, an 'assurance inflation' failure mode.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Core computability theorem; five-way final distinction (Computable/Decidable/Identifiable/ComputationallyFeasible/EpistemicallyValid); LocalFirst-DistributedWhenNecessary
b_rows_sample.statement: States the core computability theorem: KnowledgeOS core semantics are computable because its artifacts, states, transitions, and invariants can be represented finitely -- but not every question posed to it will be decidable, identifiable, or computationally feasible. Concludes a normal PC suffices for knowledge-graph operations, event processing, provenance, type checking, deterministic assurance, workflow orchestration, moderate statistical computation, local databases, and small/medium AI models; large-scale training/inference is a separate concern. States SemanticComplexity != HardwareRequirement -- hardware is determined by DataVolume, GraphSize, QueryRate, ModelSize, InferenceLatency, TrainingRequirement, Concurrency, not conceptual richness. Gives the principle LocalFirst, DistributedWhenNecessary: implement the Core on a developer workstation, benchmark it, and distribute only after observing actual bottlenecks. States the final five-way distinction that must never collapse: Computable, Decidable, Identifiable, ComputationallyFeasible, EpistemicallyValid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 69 verdict; opens Step 70 on the minimal KnowledgeOS kernel
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 69 -- PASS: 'KnowledgeOS is computationally realizable', with the progression Mathematical Semantics -> Formal Invariants -> Computational Semantics now complete. Opens Step 70 (The Minimal KnowledgeOS Kernel): deriving the smallest set of computational primitives needed to implement everything established so far, predicting convergence toward Artifact + Type + Provenance + Event + Invariant + State + Transformation + Policy, with AI/statistics/causal-inference/graph-engines/external systems operating around that kernel -- 'the first point at which we can seriously begin mapping the mathematics into an actual KnowledgeOS software architecture'.

b_aliases: Step 69 Computability, State Space and Executable Knowledge

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-computability-and-execution-boundary' POSSIBLY relates to 'computational-realizability-principle' (batch B0023). Note: Step 69's execution-boundary layer: Architecture≠Algorithm, the T:S×E→S∪Error transition formalism, Computability≠Feasibility, symbolic-representation/solver-delegation for state-space explosion, the six-item EpistemicLimit taxonomy, agent-workflow termination/execution-budget controls, Sound-vs-Complete, the five-level assurance hierarchy, and the LocalFirst-DistributedWhenNecessary deployment principle culminating in the five-way Computable/Decidable/Identifiable/Feasible/EpistemicallyValid distinction. Substantially extends computational-realizability-principle (B0020) and kos-primitive-reduction-kernel's computability section (Step 49) with new experiments and taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One Linga (active principle) engaging with two Yoni (receptive fields) represents a single proposal entering multiple fields of inquiry simultaneously. ... Configuration = L × (Y1 + Y2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the '1 Linga, 2 Yoni' configuration L x (Y1+Y2): a single proposal evaluated simultaneously by two distinct receptive fields/contexts of inquiry.

a_rows_sample.anchor: In KnowledgeOS, one assertion is evaluated in two different contexts: Context 1 (Yoni1): 'Nexus version is 3.69' -- Supported. Context 2 (Yoni2): 'Nexus version is 3.69' -- Refuted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of cross-contextual validation: the same assertion 'Nexus version is 3.69' is Supported in one context (Production) and Refuted in another (Staging), illustrating that a single proposition's evaluation can genuinely differ by context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Outcome 1 - Agreement: Consensus = Both Yoni agree. Outcome 2 - Divergence: Divergence = The two Yoni disagree ... The proposal is contested across fields. Outcome 3 - Complementarity: Complementarity = The two Yoni complement each other ... The proposal is true in different contexts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three possible outcomes when one proposal is evaluated by two fields: Agreement/Consensus (both fields concur), Divergence (fields disagree, proposal contested), and Complementarity (fields produce non-conflicting, context-relative truths).

a_rows_sample.anchor: If the two fields disagree, a reconciliation function is needed: Reconcile = (Evaluation1 + Evaluation2) / 2.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an arithmetic-average reconciliation function Reconcile=(Evaluation1+Evaluation2)/2 for disagreeing field evaluations, applied without a defined numeric encoding of qualitative evaluations like 'Supported'/'Refuted', making the averaging operation currently uninterpretable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: class Yoni: def receive(self, linga): if self.receptivity > 0.5: self.interpretation = linga.proposal ... else: self.interpretation = f'Rejected: {linga.proposal}' ... Output: Yoni1 interpretation: Nexus version is 3.69, Yoni2 interpretation: Rejected: Nexus version is 3.69.
a_rows_sample.statement: Toy Python simulation: a Yoni object accepts or rejects an incoming Linga's proposal based purely on a fixed receptivity threshold (>0.5); with receptivity 0.8 (Production) and 0.4 (Staging) applied to the same proposal, the simulation outputs acceptance in the first context and rejection in the second, illustrating context-dependent evaluation but via an unmotivated single-threshold model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = The proposition's reception in all fields ... Knowledge = L ⊕ (Y1 + Y2) ... Truth = The proposal that is accepted in all fields. ... a single truth tested in multiple fields of inquiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Closing framing: 'Truth = the proposal that is accepted in all fields' and 'Knowledge = L (direct sum) (Y1+Y2)' are offered as the deepest meaning of the configuration -- an unrigorous universal-acceptance criterion for truth, offered without formal justification, continuing this track's pattern of asserting equations rather than deriving them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Configuration = (L1 + L2 + L3) × (Y1 + Y2). This creates a 3 × 2 matrix of inquiry ... Each Linga enters both Yoni, and each Yoni receives all three Linga.
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes the proposal/field configuration to a 3x2 matrix (three proposals, two fields): Configuration=(L1+L2+L3)x(Y1+Y2), with an Argument Matrix A, Weighted Matrix W (per-proposal-per-field strength w_ij), and Evaluation Matrix E(L_i,Y_j).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A proposal may be strong in one field and weak in another: Linga1 Strong(+3)/Weak(+1) Partially validated ... Outcome 1 Consensus Across Both Fields ... Outcome 2 Divergence Across Fields ... Outcome 3 Dominance in One Field.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three outcome patterns for the 3x2 matrix: Consensus (both fields agree on ranking, truth stable across contexts), Divergence (fields disagree, truth context-dependent), and Partial Dominance (different proposals dominate different fields, truth field-specific).

b_rows_sample.anchor: def receive(self, linga): self.proposals.append(linga); evaluation = linga.strength * self.context_factor() ... Yoni1 evaluations: 3, 2, 1. Yoni2 evaluations: 2.4, 1.6, 0.8.
b_rows_sample.statement: Toy simulation: each Yoni computes evaluation=linga.strength*context_factor (context_factor=1.0 for 'Yoni1'/Production, 0.8 for 'Yoni2'/Staging); with three proposals of strength 3,2,1, Yoni1 yields evaluations 3,2,1 and Yoni2 yields 2.4,1.6,0.8 -- a uniform 0.8x scaling per field rather than a genuine content-dependent evaluation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 3 × 2 matrix is cross-validation: Each proposal is tested in each field. The truth is determined by consistent performance across fields. ... Each Yoni is a judge: Receives all proposals, Weighs all arguments, Determines the truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the 3x2 matrix as cross-validation: each proposal tested in each field, with each field cast as a 'judge' that receives, weighs, and determines truth across all proposals -- generalizing the earlier single-proposal cross-contextual-validation idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = ⊕_{i=1}^{3} ⊕_{j=1}^{2} (L_i → Y_j) ... Knowledge = The consensus across all fields. ... robust knowledge -- knowledge that survives testing in multiple contexts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closing framing: 'robust knowledge' is knowledge that survives testing/evaluation across multiple independent contexts, formalized (without derivation) as an aggregate direct-sum Truth=OplusOplus(L_i->Y_j) over all proposal-field pairs and Knowledge=the consensus across all fields.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Model 1: 1 Linga : 1 Yoni ... Fit = Low. Model 2: Multiple Linga : 1 Yoni ... Fit = Moderate. Model 3: 1 Linga : Multiple Yoni ... Fit = Moderate. Model 4: Multiple Linga : Multiple Yoni ... Fit = Very High.
b_rows_sample.statement: Compares four proposal:field configurations (1:1 single-source-single-context, N:1 multiple-sources-single-context, 1:N single-source-multiple-contexts, N:N multiple-sources-multiple-contexts) rating KnowledgeOS fit as Low, Moderate, Moderate, and Very High respectively, on the stated grounds that KnowledgeOS requires both multiple sources and multiple contexts.

Scores the four configurations on multiple-sources/cross-validation/robustness/complexity and declares Multiple-Linga x Multiple-Yoni (N:N) the best model at 5/5, on grounds it maximizes cross-validation, robustness, and generalizability while minimizing single-source bias -- despite N:N also scoring worst on complexity/efficiency.

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.62 (shared tokens: ['cross', 'field', 'multi', 'proposal', 'validation'])

a_rows_sample.anchor:
no-averaging (42.10): Pre=T, Assurance=T, Auth=T, Invariant=F
    -> Admissible = False : PASS (a 95%-admissible decision is inadmissible)
  Unknown invariant (42.12): -> None (Block) : PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision Contract admissibility (042) executes as a strict conjunction with no averaging: three true components (Pre, Assurance, Auth) plus one false component (Invariant) yields Admissible=False -- a 95%-admissible decision is inadmissible, confirming no-averaging (42.10). An Unknown invariant with the other three true yields None (Block), confirming the safety-critical policy that Unknown blocks rather than defaulting to True (42.12). In the six-fold refined form, a single failing component (Q, epistemic sufficiency) alone yields False even with the other five true. Three further falsification experiments (42.49-42.51: epistemic pass with auth fail; auth pass with hard invariant fail; safety-critical unknown) all execute to their expected results (False, False, and never-True respectively).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
under the ratified SIX-tuple (Pre,Inv,Auth,Post,Temporal,Evidence)
    there is no component typed as epistemic sufficiency, so this block
    is INEXPRESSIBLE without conflating Q into Evidence — PF-7's loss,
    executable form. Also: the ratified 6-tuple has NO ratified
    admissibility conjunction (42.9 omits Temporal; 42.41 is the
    7-tuple's law) — a formal mismatch reported to the register.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two governance-relevant findings, reported to the register rather than resolved here: (1) under the ratified Decision Contract six-tuple (Pre, Inv, Auth, Post, Temporal, Evidence), there is no component typed as epistemic sufficiency (Q), so a block on epistemic-sufficiency grounds is inexpressible without conflating Q into the Evidence component -- named PF-7's loss, here demonstrated in executable form rather than asserted in prose; (2) the ratified six-tuple has no ratified admissibility conjunction of its own -- the four-conjunct early form (42.9) omits the Temporal component, and the six-fold refined form (42.41) is actually the law for a different, seven-tuple structure -- a formal mismatch between the ratified data structure and its own admissibility law.

Two admissibility functions are implemented as three-valued (True/False/None) strict conjunctions, never averaged: adm_early(pre, inv, assur, auth) per 042 section 42.9 (four conjuncts: Precondition, Invariant, Assurance, Authorization) and adm_refined(P, I, A, E, Q, T) per 042 section 42.41 (six conjuncts including Q, epistemic sufficiency, and T, Temporal). Both share the same policy: if any component is False, the result is False; else if any component is None (Unknown), the result is None (interpreted as Block for safety-critical decisions); only if all components are True is the result True. The script's own docstring and inline notes flag that the ratified Decision Contract data structure is a six-tuple (Pre, Inv, Auth, Post, Temporal, Evidence) that matches neither adm_early (which omits Temporal) nor adm_refined (whose six conjuncts belong to a different seven-tuple structure, and which includes Q, a component absent from the ratified six-tuple) -- so the ratified six-tuple currently has no ratified admissibility conjunction of its own, reported to the register as a formal mismatch rather than resolved here.

a_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: DEL's S5/T semantics impose veridicality (K_i-phi implies phi), but the corpus's Closure-03 result 'Admission is not a truth function' means an admitted/supported assertion can be false and must be retained precisely to explain how it came to be wrong; therefore mapping the corpus's Supported/Refuted status pair Sigma onto the knowledge operator K_i imports veridicality and contradicts a boxed corpus result -- the weaker KD45 (belief, no T) avoids this but fails on a separate ground (Conflict/D).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict is a well-formed KnowledgeOS state and an inconsistency in every normal epistemic logic with D.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: under axiom D (present in both KD45 and S5), K_i-phi AND K_i-not-phi is unsatisfiable, but the corpus treats Sigma=(1,1) Conflict as a normal, persistent state with no rule forcing its resolution; hosting Conflict therefore requires dropping axiom D entirely, i.e. moving to a paraconsistent or non-adjunctive epistemic logic, which is a different framework from DEL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V is total: every proposition has a truth value at every world. So DEL can express ignorance but cannot distinguish M1 not-asked / M2 asked-absent / M3 asked-insufficient. All three collapse. This is exactly Critical Failure #7.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the corpus's own prior 'pi problem' critique of DEL: because DEL's valuation V is total, the framework can express bare ignorance (not-K-phi and not-K-not-phi) but cannot distinguish 'not asked', 'asked and absent', and 'asked and insufficient' -- exactly the corpus's Critical Failure #7 empirically found at Step 280; notes both frameworks fix this the same way (KnowledgeOS via Q_t, DEL via the awareness set A_i).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_i is closed under consequence. Measured: Cn(.) = 0 occurrences in both lanes. A is a set of asserted items, not a theory. ... A is a belief base, not a belief set.
a_rows_sample.statement: Logical omniscience (DEL's K_i is closed under valid consequence) is incompatible with the corpus's unclosed assertion set: measured zero occurrences of a consequence-closure operator Cn(.) in the corpus, so the corpus's assertion set A is a belief base (a set of individually asserted items) rather than a belief set (closed under entailment) -- a structural carrier-level mismatch prior to any consideration of dynamics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Admission is governed -- LLM proposes; Lord evaluates; Governance authorizes. DEL has no place to attach an authority predicate to an update.

a_rows_sample.statement: States five falsifiable hypotheses with named falsifiers: DEL-H1 (Q_t cong A_i is an exact isomorphism, falsified by a non-representable Q_t state or an unreconstructible awareness structure); DEL-H2 (no sound embedding of Sigma into any normal modal logic with D preserves Conflict as satisfiable, falsified by exhibiting one); DEL-H3 (the corpus's M1/M2/M3 missingness distinction under Q_t is exactly the explicit/implicit-knowledge distinction, falsified by a fourth Q_t-distinction with no awareness counterpart); DEL-H4 (adopting S5 for Sigma would falsify a boxed corpus result, trivially checkable); DEL-H5 (the corpus's Revision = EventAddition + StateReDerivation is not DEL's product update, since product update only ever restricts W, falsified by exhibiting a RevisionType that is a pure restriction).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PARTIALLY COMPATIBLE — as a regime over Q_t, not as a foundation for Sigma ... This sharpens it: the regime it can support is awareness, and the part it cannot support is Sigma.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: DEL is partially compatible with KnowledgeOS -- exact and compatible at one point (Q_t cong A_i, independently converged upon), incompatible at the centre (Sigma is not K_i because of veridicality, and Conflict is an inconsistency under D), and carrier-mismatched (belief base vs belief set); explicitly reconciled with, and sharpening, the corpus's own 2026-08-25 position that DEL may be 'a reasoning regime KnowledgeOS may support; not the Kernel' -- the supportable regime is specifically awareness, not Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero <-> an antichain of unsatisfied requirements in a finite lattice — an ORDER, not a NUMBER
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds Zero(K,G,EC) (evaluated over a finite requirement set with sufficiency rules Gamma, returning one of ten statuses per requirement, boxed 'Zero != simple subtraction') fits Shannon's measure-free structural layer: requirements generate a finite meet-semilattice under partition refinement, and Zero is the set of requirements not yet in the satisfied down-set -- an antichain in a lattice, an ORDER rather than a NUMBER; the corpus's own boxed rejection of simple subtraction is exactly the statement that this lattice is not a measure, stated without the vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: |gaps(A)| = |gaps(B)| = 2, yet A != B as work plans — any count/scalar conflates them. That is a demonstration that Zero is not a cardinality, i.e. not a measure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports an executed corroboration from zero_reference.py: two work plans A and B have equal gap-counts (|gaps(A)|=|gaps(B)|=2) yet are different work plans, so any scalar/cardinality summary of Zero conflates them -- an independent demonstration (found by running code, not by information-theoretic argument) that Zero cannot be a cardinality/measure, agreeing with the information-theory finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H, I, D_KL are all functionals of a probability distribution. (Omega,F,P) as a triple: 0 occurrences in both lanes; T-3 rules probability not required. Shannon's quantitative layer is unavailable to KnowledgeOS by the same ruling that declined probability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: Shannon entropy, mutual information and KL-divergence are all functionals of a declared probability distribution (Omega,F,P), which has zero occurrences in the corpus and was explicitly ruled unnecessary by Step 282's T-3; therefore the entire Shannon quantitative layer is unavailable to KnowledgeOS by the same ruling that declined probability, leaving only the measure-free lattice layer (which supports refinement/coverage/gap structure but no number).

b_rows_sample.anchor: entropy appears 87 times in the corpus, 0 ratified. ... every one of those 87 uses is either (a) metaphorical, (b) about an external regime not adopted, or (c) an error.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measures 87 corpus occurrences of the word 'entropy'/'entropy H(' with zero ratified formal uses, and infers (recorded as unaudited hypothesis IT-H1, not an asserted fact) that every occurrence must be metaphorical, about an unadopted external regime, or an error, since no probability distribution exists anywhere in the corpus to license a genuine Shannon entropy computation; classifies this as the same defect class as prior findings about quantitative vocabulary used without the structure that licenses it, noting the corpus's own Shannon extraction already warns 'information is not meaning is not knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion with Sigma=(0,1) Refuted is a first-class member of A and, on the veridicality thesis, carries no semantic information at all. Adopting Floridi would make Refuted inexpressible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: Floridi's veridicality thesis holds semantic information is necessarily truthful (false 'information' is not information), but the corpus's Closure-03 result 'Admission is not a truth function' deliberately retains Refuted assertions as first-class members of A; adopting Floridi's thesis would make Refuted assertions inexpressible -- classified as the same shape of error as adopting S5 veridicality for Sigma in the DEL comparison document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dretske's definition is strictly stronger — it requires (i) a conditional probability, (ii) its value to be exactly 1, and (iii) a background-knowledge index k. KnowledgeOS supplies none.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds Dretske's information-carrying definition (signal r carries the information that s is F iff the conditional probability of s-is-F given r and receiver prior knowledge k equals exactly 1) strictly stronger than what KnowledgeOS's Evidence(O,P,C,R) (a relevance relation under a rule) can supply, especially since the verification-lane Qualify function has no implemented body (TG-14); concludes Evidence is not Dretskean information-carrying and cannot become so without reversing the T-3 no-probability ruling.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a way to distinguish not-asked from asked-and-empty | tolerance of contradictory signals as a state | provenance/authority | a goal state | non-veridical carriers ... a source distribution | a channel | an empirical relational structure | a code/compression notion
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists missing primitives on the information-theory side needed to host KnowledgeOS (a way to distinguish not-asked from asked-and-empty, since a sample-space partition has no 'unasked' cell -- the same defect class found against DEL; tolerance of contradictory signals as a state, for Conflict; provenance/authority, for governed admission; a goal state, for Ideal State; non-veridical carriers, for Refuted assertions) and on the KnowledgeOS side needed to host information theory (a source distribution -- 0 occurrences, declined by T-3; a channel -- no P(O|phi) anywhere; an empirical relational structure -- corpus finding G-12 blocks any numeric information measure independently of T-3; a code/compression notion -- absent and not obviously needed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: IT-H1 ... IT-H2 ... IT-H3 ... IT-H4 ... IT-H5
b_rows_sample.statement: States five falsifiable hypotheses: IT-H1 (all 87 corpus 'entropy' uses are metaphorical/regime-external/erroneous, falsified by exhibiting one that declares (Omega,F,P) and computes H over it); IT-H2 (Zero is a lattice antichain, not a measure -- no scalar summary preserves the ten-status distinction, already partly corroborated by zero_reference.py); IT-H3 (no distance-to-Ideal-State satisfying Q12 is definable without a metric or distribution, neither of which exists); IT-H4 (adopting Floridi veridicality would make Refuted inexpressible); IT-H5 (Evidence(O,P,C,R) is strictly weaker than Dretskean information-carrying, falsified by deriving Dretske's conditional-probability-1 condition from Qualify, currently impossible since Qualify has no body).

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE WEAKEST FIT OF THE FIVE — the quantitative layer is unavailable and the semantic layer contradicts a boxed corpus result ... What this analysis adds is that the residue is a lattice, and that Zero is already sitting in it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: information theory is the weakest fit of the five external theories compared in this series -- no entropy/mutual-information/KL is available (all require the declined distribution), Floridi's veridicality thesis directly contradicts the corpus's Admission-is-not-a-truth-function result, and Dretske needs a channel and independence/prior structure the corpus lacks -- but the measure-free partition/coverage lattice does exactly fit Zero, and the corpus's own 2026-08-25 conclusion ('information is not meaning is not knowledge') is endorsed as correct; the analysis's own addition is identifying that the surviving residue is specifically a LATTICE, and that Zero already sits in it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: context_preserved = 1.000 should never appear as 'The experiment demonstrated perfect context preservation.' It means: 'The operator was designed to preserve context.' ... A design property is not an empirical result. ... Could this number have been different if the experiment produced a different o
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes several audit corrections (saturation at budget 40, Z5 improperly collapsing state and observable, untested requirements 6/7, a definitional restriction-on-cross-dimension result, and context_preserved=1.000 being a design property) into a permanent methodological rule: a metric that could not have come out differently given the operator's own design is a design property, not an empirical result; proposes a litmus test ('could this number have been different if the experiment produced a different outcome?') and mandates a DEGENERATE METRICS section in every future experiment report.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A measurement that cannot vary cannot establish the property it purports to measure. That should probably become a permanent experimental validity invariant in KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, as a candidate permanent experimental-validity invariant for KnowledgeOS, the principle that a measurement which cannot vary under the tested manipulation cannot establish the property it purports to measure -- generalizing the exposed_structure_differs=0/4368 degeneracy finding into a reusable methodological rule.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'design-property-not-empirical-result-rule' POSSIBLY relates to 'measurement-cannot-vary-invariant' (batch B0067). Note: A permanent methodological rule distinguishing design properties (results forced by the operator's own construction) from genuine empirical findings, mandating a dedicated report section; closely related to the measurement-cannot-vary-invariant recorded in S2807.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the five realized S1–S5 structural checks are run over the migration plan as it stood at each historical commit and must reproduce the defects the independent reviews raised — and must be QUIET on the repaired current artifact
a_rows_sample.statement: A falsification back-test materializes three historical git states of the migration plan (AMD4/AMD5/AMD6 commits) and runs five realized structural checks (S1-S5) over each; the matrix correctly reproduces the historical defects (DI-1, DI-2, DI-5, DI-7, DI-4) at the states where independent reviewers found them and is quiet (never falsely PASS) on the corrected AMD6 state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: mechanical assurance proves DECLARED STRUCTURE — identifier uniqueness, intra-document reference resolution, declared vocabulary, table shape, disposition labelling. It does NOT check soundness, completeness, authority, or provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: The D-4 statement, carried verbatim on every report: mechanical assurance proves declared structure only; it cannot discover an undeclared architectural act (the missing-act class, e.g. RD-1, RD-7, RD-3·b), which is caught only by human Architecture review — 'a PASS here is mechanical, not architectural, assurance.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: DI-3/DI-6 enumeration-vs-content agreement ... NOT-CHECKED. No catalogued capability owns the class. Named as OQ-1 and returned to Governance/ARB
a_rows_sample.statement: A required back-test target (a stated count contradicting the rows it counts, e.g. DI-3/DI-6) is deliberately NOT built because no catalogued capability owns that class of check; the gap is returned to governance as an open question rather than an ad-hoc capability being invented to close it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: copy the clean (AMD6) artifact, introduce ONE defect per copy, run the adapter over the directory ... every verdict flipped, with correct line evidence, and unmutated copies stayed PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: A mutation-testing methodology (one injected defect per otherwise-clean artifact copy) is used to demonstrate the checkers are content-driven rather than canned: a single heading collision produces both a direct S1 duplicate-identifier failure and a cascading S2 reference-ambiguity failure across ~20 citation sites, an added dangling step reference correctly triggers S2, a dropped table cell correctly triggers S4, and unmutated control copies stay PASS in every slice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V-2 ... FIVE LIVE TRUE POSITIVES, and they had survived every review that passed over them ... The implementation design passed the Governance review and three independent Architecture reviews with a malformed table in it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Running the checker over already-reviewed governed documents (not test fixtures) surfaces five real, previously-uncaught table-shape defects, including one in the implementation-design document that had already passed a Governance review and three independent Architecture reviews — the program's first operational evidence not obtained via a back-test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V-3 ... S2 CANNOT DISTINGUISH DEFINING an enumeration from QUOTING one — a systematic false-positive class over review artifacts ... this very verification report ... it parsed an enumeration I QUOTED as one I DEFINED
a_rows_sample.statement: Measuring the S2 reference-check over 83 review documents finds 9 false-positive FAILs (including all four AMD architecture reviews and this very verification report, which misread its own quoted enumeration as a defining one), because S2 cannot yet distinguish a document that DEFINES an enumeration from one that merely CITES/QUOTES it — a rule-scope gap to be raised as an open question, not silently suppressed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V-4 ... EKS-06 IS ALREADY TAKEN — and the brainstorming document still assumes it is free ... a live DP-1/PMR-10 collision waiting to happen.
a_rows_sample.statement: An identifier EKS-06 was minted for one problem (reference resolution) at 14:35 the same day, while a separate brainstorming document and its review both independently propose 'EKS-06' for a different problem (governance-assurance/role-execution scaling); the mint is also uncommitted (invisible to git and to any collision check), constituting a live identifier-collision risk.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanical Assurance proves DECLARED STRUCTURE / Architecture Review discovers UNDECLARED ARCHITECTURAL CONTENT.
a_rows_sample.statement: An addendum records the Decision Authority's own refinement of the mechanical/architectural boundary, framing it as a division of labour rather than a limitation, and explicitly forbidding the platform from ever claiming 'mechanical assurance proves architectural completeness.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: nine required elements ... aggregate verdict: [FAIL] — fail-closed, never PASS on silence
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a nine-element handoff assurance report (artifact identity, checker/version/commit, checks executed, aggregate result, findings-with-evidence, evidence locations, NOT-CHECKED areas, known limitations, timestamp/execution context) with a fail-closed aggregate-verdict precedence rule FAIL > INCONCLUSIVE > WARN > PASS, discovered and repaired as a CLI-test finding during implementation (an INCONCLUSIVE slice preceding a FAIL could otherwise mask it).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AMD4 ... FAIL ... AMD5 ... FAIL ... AMD6 ... INCONCLUSIVE ... New authoring draft ... FAIL ... Same draft, remediated ... INCONCLUSIVE
a_rows_sample.statement: Real-corpus validation of the author-side handoff report across five runs (defective AMD4, defective AMD5, corrected AMD6 without a vocabulary config, a fresh defective authoring draft, and the same draft remediated) shows the expected fail/pass pattern in every case, with the tool refusing PASS even after remediation on slices it cannot fully assess (fail-closed by construction), and zero false positives on the corrected AMD6 state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OBSERVED (measured in the record, cited) ... ESTIMATED (clearly labelled — not measured) ... UNKNOWN (not measured, not invented)
a_rows_sample.statement: Business-value reporting discipline: claims are strictly separated into OBSERVED (measured, cited), ESTIMATED (explicitly labelled as an estimate derived from observed chain volume, e.g. 'per-defect cost is closer to one amendment cycle than one reviewer minute'), and UNKNOWN (explicitly not measured and not invented, e.g. reviewer-hour or financial savings, or whether authors will voluntarily run a warn-only checker).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-AIP-GOV-STATE-DURABILITY should be the FIRST real consumer of the deterministic assurance capability — not a second project that waits until durability is finished.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends that the durability migration work become the first real consumer of the deterministic assurance capability rather than a separate, sequential project, arguing the two tracks already share an evidence base (the migration corpus is the checker's own back-test corpus), making integration a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance root resolution must FOLLOW the governed evidence boundary; it must not DEFINE or OWN that boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the one load-bearing coupling rule between the two tracks: the assurance checker's root-resolution mechanism must follow wherever the governed evidence boundary is placed by B', never define or own that boundary itself, so ownership of the boundary stays exclusively with the durability decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-1 ... The checker must remain WARN-ONLY initially ... G-2 ... The checker cannot discover an undeclared architectural act ... G-4 ... No authority manufacture
a_rows_sample.statement: Six load-bearing guardrails (G-1..G-6) for integrating the checker: warn-only with no gate/hook/CI wiring; inability to discover undeclared architectural acts; every report states what it did not check positively; no authority manufacture (only CONFLICT DETECTED, never INDEPENDENCE = TRUE); no frontmatter/card requirement riding along; no identifier minted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Automation may reduce assurance cost but must never manufacture authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: The core invariant proposed to govern all governance-role cost optimization: automation may replace mechanical proof-of-fact work, but independence, architectural judgement, acceptance, and capability/ownership establishment remain human-authority boundaries.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the timing question is already ruled — in both directions ... Deterministic checks ... Now ... Assurance classes ... risk routing ... gates ... Backlog + a PO/ARB act
b_rows_sample.statement: An independent review of the cost-optimization proposal splits it into two programmes governed by different rules: deterministic read-only checks may proceed now (no new authority, matches the 2026-08-04 accepted correction that automation of deterministic work is not speculative architecture), while assurance-class/risk-routing/gate changes are frozen under the 2026-08-01 methodology freeze because the deficiency motivating them is in KnowledgeOS governance execution, not PublicDigit implementation, so the freeze's exception does not fire.

b_rows_sample.anchor: knowledge-lint.php is a 343-line 'PHPStan for knowledge' that is hard-scoped to docs/knowledge/ ... and never sees docs/knowledgeos/. That single scope gap is why the entire Track 2 corpus had zero mechanical coverage.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a concrete, measured tooling gap: the existing knowledge-lint mechanical assurance checker never scans docs/knowledgeos, so recommends extending it with a profile plus a new root rather than building nine new 'engines.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: The durability migration chain (AMD3→AMD6) is literally the test corpus the assurance checker is being built to back-test against, and the checker's job list is literally the migration's own mandated pre-delivery verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds that the two seemingly separate work items (cost-optimization/deterministic-assurance, and the durability migration) already share the same evidence base and back-test corpus, so integration is a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem; the checker must remain warn-only through Phase 1 to avoid itself becoming a governance object requiring authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Keep-apart list (G-4, corpus): Recording ≠ Asserting · Evidence ≠ Proof · Reference ≠ Ownership · Author ≠ Independent Reviewer · Self-check ≠ Independent Assurance · Execution ≠ Governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the estate's six-item keep-apart discipline as ESTABLISHED, cited as the invariant set the deterministic-assurance capability must never violate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance as capability vs context: corpus treats deterministic assurance as a cross-cutting capability; the event-driven refinement proposes a new Assurance Context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T2: two competing framings of deterministic assurance (cross-cutting capability vs a new bounded Assurance Context) coexist unreconciled across the corpus.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Yes — with partial operations and explicit epistemic types. The word partial is crucial
a_rows_sample.statement: States that KnowledgeOS can be a formal composable/revisable system precisely because operations are partial, allowing 'operation undefined' rather than invented results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observe:W\rightarrow\mathcal O ... Infer:\mathcal E\rightharpoonup\mathcal A ... Validate:\mathcal A\times\mathcal E\rightarrow\mathcal V
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines eight typed operations between universe subsets, several explicitly partial.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Infer(E)=\bot ... \bot\neq False. And \bot\neq Unknown ... no justified result exists under the specified inference system
a_rows_sample.statement: States a total Infer would encourage hallucination on insufficient evidence, defining bottom as a distinct non-result: bottom≠False, bottom≠Unknown.

a_rows_sample.anchor: False: H=False ... Unknown: Unknown(H) ... Undefined: f(x)=\bot ... False\neq Unknown\neq Undefined
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally distinguishes three failure states as mathematically distinct: False, Unknown, and Undefined.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hypothesis, SupportedClaim, ValidatedClaim, Forecast, DecisionCandidate, AuthorizedAction ... These are not simply statuses. They determine what operations are permitted
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces epistemic types that determine, not merely describe, which operations are permitted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Promote:Hypothesis\times Evidence\rightharpoonup SupportedClaim ... a hypothesis does not automatically become supported merely because an LLM produced it
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an admissible type-promotion operation from Hypothesis to SupportedClaim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hypothesis\notin Domain(Execute) ... EpistemicTypeError. This is the epistemic equivalent of a programming type error
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines epistemic type safety via domain membership, giving EpistemicTypeError.

a_rows_sample.anchor: World\rightarrow Knowledge\rightarrow Action\rightarrow World ... OperationalCycle from EpistemicCircularity
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes a legitimate operational cycle from problematic epistemic circularity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: g\circ f only when Range(f)\subseteq Domain(g) ... SemanticTypeCompatibility is a precondition for composition
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines composition validity and the epistemic composition law of semantic type compatibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RiskModel\circ Infer is not a valid composition ... Evidence\rightarrow Inference\rightarrow Validation\rightarrow Model\rightarrow Decision ... rather than Evidence\rightarrow LLM\rightarrow Decision ... a major architectural strengthening
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing an invalid composition requires an intervening Validate step, giving a stronger assurance path than direct LLM-to-decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: id_X(x)=x ... identity element for composition
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an identity transformation giving the algebra an identity element.

a_rows_sample.anchor: h\circ(g\circ f)=(h\circ g)\circ f ... PureTransformation from StateTransition
a_rows_sample.statement: States expected associativity for pure composition while requiring PureTransformation to be distinguished from StateTransition, worked with unit-conversion vs ApproveChange examples.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (\mathcal K,\circ,\oplus,\ldots) algebra of knowledge objects ... (K_t,event)\rightarrow K_{t+1} algebra of state transitions ... should not be conflated
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes two distinct mathematical layers that should not be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Merge:K\times K\rightharpoonup K' ... Clean merge K_1\oplus K_2=K_3 ... Merge with conflict K_3+ConflictSet ... Unmergeable Merge=\bot
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines partial knowledge merge with three possible outcomes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_1\preceq K_2 ... must not mean K_2 is more correct. It means K_2 contains at least as much represented information ... MoreInformation\neq MoreTruth
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an information ordering explicitly distinct from a truth ordering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_1\sqsubseteq K_2 refinement (adds information without violating K_1's semantics) ... K_1\xrightarrow{E}K_2 revision (previous commitments may be defeated)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines knowledge refinement distinct from revision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Combine(E_1,E_2) requires knowledge of Dependence(E_1,E_2) ... the provenance graph becomes mathematically important
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires evidence dependence knowledge for combination, mathematically connecting the provenance graph to aggregation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: independence is a property of the evidence-generation process ... should not assume E_1\perp E_2 merely because the records have different IDs
a_rows_sample.statement: States independence is contextual, a property of the evidence-generation process, not assumable from mere record-ID difference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BayesianUpdate, LikelihoodRatio, DeterministicConjunction, SetUnion, ExpertAggregation ... EvidenceAggregation is bounded-context specific
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists five non-universal evidence-aggregation rules, giving EvidenceAggregation as bounded-context specific.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_1\preceq K_2\Rightarrow f(K_1)\preceq f(K_2) ... adding independent evidence [monotonic] ... K\models A, new evidence E\models\neg A, K'\not\models A [non-monotonic]
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines monotonicity, worked with both a monotonic and a non-monotonic example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence_total = Confidence_1 x Confidence_2 x Confidence_3 ... That is generally wrong
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects naive multiplication of stage confidences as generally wrong; the correct propagation depends on uncertainty semantics and dependence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Measurement uncertainty, Sampling uncertainty, Parameter uncertainty, Model uncertainty, Prediction uncertainty, Epistemic uncertainty, Aleatory variability ... must not automatically be collapsed into one number
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes at least seven kinds of uncertainty that must not be collapsed into one number.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Aleatory variability: Variation inherent in the phenomenon ... Epistemic uncertainty: Uncertainty caused by incomplete knowledge ... Randomness != LackOfKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the aleatory-vs-epistemic distinction with a travel-time/traffic example, giving the principle Randomness != LackOfKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Y=X+epsilon ... E[epsilon]=0 and Var(epsilon)=sigma^2 ... those assumptions themselves require justification
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a basic measurement-error model and warns its moment assumptions require justification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Y=h(X,theta,epsilon) ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the measurement model where available
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes to a measurement model KnowledgeOS should preserve, else downstream models may treat measured values as exact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Var(Y) approx J Sigma J^T ... Jacobian ... covariance matrix ... exposes why independent multiplication of confidence values is inadequate
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes first-order error propagation via the Jacobian and covariance matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cov(X_i,X_j) != 0 ... Var(X+Y)=Var(X)+Var(Y)+2Cov(X,Y) ... Dependence matters
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes covariance's role in propagation, giving the principle that dependence matters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 and E_2 both come from the same underlying report. Treating them as independent could artificially increase certainty. This is a major risk in AI systems
b_rows_sample.statement: States the evidence-duplication problem as a major risk in AI systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1=f(S), E_2=g(S) ... E_1 not-perp E_2 ... combining them as independent evidence is invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes correlated evidence sharing a common source and invalidates treating it as independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance -> DependenceStructure -> CorrectUncertaintyPropagation ... This is a major result
b_rows_sample.statement: States provenance's mathematical role: it enables estimating dependency and hence correct uncertainty propagation, called a major result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(H|E) = P(E|H)P(H)/P(E) ... prior P(H) and likelihood P(E|H) must have explicit provenance and assumptions
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Bayesian updating and requires explicit provenance/assumptions for prior and likelihood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Not every knowledge problem has a meaningful prior ... BayesianUpdate must be a typed operation requiring a valid probabilistic model. It should not be the universal inference engine
b_rows_sample.statement: Constrains Bayesian updating to be a typed operation requiring a valid model, not a universal inference engine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: confidence intervals; sampling distributions; hypothesis tests; bootstrap distributions; asymptotic approximations ... theta-hat +- z SE(theta-hat) ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the framework
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists frequentist uncertainty representations and requires preserving the inferential framework used.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A standard confidence interval [L,U] should not automatically be interpreted as P(L<=theta<=U)=0.95. That interpretation is generally Bayesian, not classical frequentist
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against the common misinterpretation of a frequentist confidence interval as a Bayesian probability statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in [L,U] ... Latency in [100ms,150ms] ... No probability distribution is required
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines interval uncertainty requiring no probability distribution, with a latency example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in S where S is a feasible set ... useful when evidence constrains the possibilities without assigning probabilities
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes interval uncertainty to set-valued uncertainty over a feasible set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in [0,100] but have no justified distribution. The system should not invent X~Uniform(0,100) ... Bounded != Probabilistically Specified
b_rows_sample.statement: Forbids inventing a uniform distribution over a bounded but unjustified range, giving the principle Bounded != Probabilistically Specified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: theta in Theta_I ... PartiallyIdentified. This is stronger than simply saying uncertain
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces partial identification as a distinct, stronger-than-generic-uncertainty statistical concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10<=X<=20 and Y=2X ... 20<=Y<=40 ... propagated a set-valued constraint without inventing a probability distribution
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of set-valued constraint propagation without inventing a distribution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_1,X_2 -> Y -> Z ... KnowledgeOS should preserve DependencyGraph. Then uncertainty can be propagated through the graph
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a dependency graph structure for propagating uncertainty through a network.
