They are FIVE DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING crammed into one field. Once separated, the epistemic core is uniquely determined at
a_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the verifier's own prior escalation of the status-vocabulary question to the author (B1 in S1605): the framing of 'competing vocabularies' was itself malformed, since the 11+ terms are not alternatives for one dimension but instances of 5 different kinds of thing conflated into a single field; once separated, the true epistemic core is uniquely determined at 3 states.

a_rows_sample.anchor: All discovered vocabularies (executed enumeration, 24 terms) [table with file counts and numbered-step spans, e.g. Unknown 45 files/steps 12..242, Supported 24/8..245, ...]
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes a corpus-wide enumeration finding 24 distinct status-like terms in use (Unknown, Supported, Rejected, Inferred, Candidate, Observed, Accepted, Confirmed, Superseded, Conflicted, Approved, Validated, Refuted, Proposed, Contested, Established, Corroborated, Verified, Disputed, Determined, Authoritative, Deprecated, Retired, and their file/step-span counts) -- the empirical basis for the subsequent semantic classification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test applied to every term: is it a property of ONE assertion, a relation between TWO, a lifecycle marker, a governance act, or derivable from the others? [5 categories: STATE n=3 Unknown/Supported/Refuted; DERIVED n=5; RELATION(binary) n=4; LIFECYCLE n=4; GOVERNANCE n=7; COLLISION n=1 Determined]
a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies all 24 discovered terms via a 5-way decisive test (unary epistemic property vs binary relation vs lifecycle marker vs governance act vs derivable-from-others) into: 3 irreducible unary epistemic states (Unknown, Supported, Refuted), 5 derived values (Conflicted, Observed, Established, Inferred, Confirmed), 4 binary relations (Superseded, Contested, Corroborated, Disputed), 4 lifecycle markers (Proposed, Candidate, Deprecated, Retired), 7 governance acts (Approved, Rejected, Accepted, Validated, Verified, Authoritative, Invalidated), and 1 genuine terminological collision (Determined).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Superseded is a RELATION, not a state. It requires two assertions. Step 218.21 states this itself: C1 --superseded--> C2, not delete(C1). ... Deprecated is explicitly NOT epistemic -- step-218.22 boxes Deprecated != Falsified. ... Observed and Inferred differ by EVIDENCE TYPE, not epistemic state. .
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the decisive individual justifications behind the classification, each grounded in corpus citation: Superseded requires two assertions (step-218.21's C1-->superseded-->C2, never a delete); Deprecated is explicitly non-epistemic per step-218.22 (Deprecated != Falsified); Observed and Inferred both mean Supported but differ only in evidence type (belongs in E, not Sigma); Established reduces to Supported plus an uncodified corroboration threshold with no distinguishing operation; Determined is a genuine terminological collision (a status at steps 186-189, an aggregate at step 196.26).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I proposed a four-state set (Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted). That is one too many. Conflicted(A,K) := exists A' in K: same (subject,predicate), different object, overlapping validity, same context, neither Refuted. Conflicted is computable from the state. No operation requires it as a stored
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a previously proposed 4-state Sigma set (adding Conflicted) down to a minimal 3-state Sigma={Unknown, Supported, Refuted}, by giving an explicit computable definition of Conflicted(A,K) as a derived predicate over the state (same subject/predicate, differing object, overlapping validity, same context, neither Refuted) that no operation requires as a stored primitive, and warning that storing it duplicates derivable information and risks an update anomaly (stored flag disagreeing with computed value).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4-state (adds Conflicted): REFUTED as minimal. 6-state historical (Proposed/Supported/Established/Superseded/Contested/Invalidated): REFUTED -- mixes four categories ... Only Supported is an epistemic state, and Contested is a relation. Two orthogonal dimensions: CONFIRMED. 3-state core + separate d
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests and refutes two larger candidate status sets: a 4-state candidate (Conflicted refuted as derived, per the prior finding) and a 6-state 'historical' candidate (Proposed/Supported/Established/Superseded/Contested/Invalidated) which is shown to mix all 5 category types at once (lifecycle, epistemic, derived, relation, governance) with only Supported actually being an epistemic state; the surviving candidate is a 3-state epistemic core plus separate orthogonal dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma perp Gamma -- orthogonality CONFIRMED by construction. All four quadrants are meaningful and occur in the domain: [Supported/not-approved; Unknown/permitted; Refuted/still-authoritative; Supported/rejected]. Corpus support: step-194.19 boxes EpistemicStrength != GovernanceStatus; step-008 sepa
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms by explicit 2x2 construction that epistemic status (Sigma) and governance status (Gamma) are orthogonal dimensions: all four quadrant combinations (Supported+not-approved; Unknown+permitted; Refuted+still-authoritative; Supported+rejected) correspond to meaningful, realistic domain cases, and the corpus itself states the separation (step-194.19: EpistemicStrength != GovernanceStatus; step-008: acceptance vs commitment; step-232.4: Validation->Assessment) even though it then violates it by storing governance terms inside Sigma.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion A=(id,P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi) with Sigma in {Unknown,Supported,Refuted}. Gamma governance: separate, attached to the governance context -- not to A. Superseded: a relation in R or in History -- not a value of Sigma. Valid(K): the blocking sub-predicate was state consistency, which needed a vocab
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives the operational consequences of the 3-state Sigma resolution: the Assertion tuple becomes A=(id,P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi) with Sigma restricted to {Unknown,Supported,Refuted}; Gamma (governance) attaches separately to a governance context, not to A; Superseded becomes a relation in R or History rather than a Sigma value; the previously blocked state-consistency sub-predicate of Valid(K) (from S1603/S1605) becomes computable now that Sigma is fixed; Merge/Supersede become well-typed since supersession operates on the relation rather than mutating a status field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t shape: relations must live somewhere -- this constrains the container. UL: 24 terms reduce to 3 states + 4 relations + 7 governance + 4 lifecycle. The 'eleven vocabularies' dissolve.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes a downstream constraint on the still-open K_t shape blocker (B2): since relations (Superseded, Contested, Corroborated, Disputed) now need an explicit home in the container, this constrains what K_t's tuple/shape can be; and restates the overall UL resolution -- the notorious 'eleven competing vocabularies' dissolve into a clean 3+4+7+4 partition (states + relations + governance + lifecycle).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended canonical model: Sigma: Assertion -> {Unknown,Supported,Refuted} epistemic, minimal, DERIVED from Assessment. Gamma: Assertion x GovernanceContext -> GovernanceStatus, governance, separate dimension. R subseteq AxA: supersedes, contests, corroborates, disputes. Lifecycle: metadata, not e
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the final canonical model for the epistemic/governance/relation/lifecycle split: Sigma:Assertion->{Unknown,Supported,Refuted} (derived from Assessment); Gamma:Assertion x GovernanceContext -> GovernanceStatus (a separate dimension); R subseteq AxA carrying supersedes/contests/corroborates/disputes; Lifecycle as non-epistemic metadata -- classified overall as DERIVED (from corpus evidence plus executed classification and minimality tests), not a normative proposal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Not Sigma. Sigma is determined at three states by the mathematics and the corpus. The one residue: Gamma's value set ... That is a governance-process question, not a mathematical one, and it does not block the formal theory ... Therefore I am NOT asking the author to decide anything yet.
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes the B1 blocker without escalating to the human author: Sigma itself is now fully derived (not normative), and the only residual open item -- Gamma's own value vocabulary (which governance statuses the domain recognizes) -- is explicitly deferred as a later, non-blocking governance-process question rather than treated as an immediate normative decision, correcting the S1605 escalation of B1 to AUTHOR INPUT REQUIRED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Downstream effect: B1 is resolved. The next load-bearing gap moves to K_t's shape -- and Section 9 has just constrained it, because relations (R) now provably need a home.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the downstream effect of closing B1: the single remaining load-bearing (normative) blocker from S1605's matrix becomes B2, K_t's tuple shape -- now further constrained by the requirement that relations R have an explicit home in the container.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TIER 1 -- DELIVERED UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME (substance exists) -- 24 [examples: MATHEMATICAL-KERNEL-REVERIFICATION -> KERNEL-AUDIT-230-232 + KERNEL-RECONCILIATION-230-236; K-EQUALITY-AND-IDENTITY-AUDIT -> IDENTITY-ROUNDTRIP-AUDIT; EPISTEMIC-STATUS-RECONCILIATION -> DECISION-SIGMA-EPISTEMIC-STATUS]
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies 24 of the 93 nominally missing artifacts as actually delivered under different filenames (e.g. the demanded EPISTEMIC-STATUS-RECONCILIATION.md was in fact delivered as DECISION-SIGMA-EPISTEMIC-STATUS.md, i.e. S1606; K-EQUALITY-AND-IDENTITY-AUDIT.md as IDENTITY-ROUNDTRIP-AUDIT.md, i.e. S1600), and notes one demanded artifact class (216-STEP-* files) is now superseded outright since the corpus has grown to 246 steps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H1 -- One canonical finite status set ... H2 -- Status is multidimensional [EpistemicStatus vs GovernanceStatus, also evidential/validity/lifecycle/governance status] ... Determine whether the historical '11 competing vocabularies' are actually different dimensions that were incorrectly collapsed in
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 4 explicit, mutually-non-exclusive hypotheses to test regarding epistemic status (H1: one canonical finite set is mathematically required; H2: status is genuinely multidimensional, with the '11 competing vocabularies' possibly being distinct dimensions incorrectly collapsed into one field; H3: status is context-dependent, requiring a parameterized algebra; H4: status is partly derived rather than stored) -- H2 and H4 are exactly what S1606's subsequent analysis independently confirms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H1 one canonical finite status set: REFUTED -- the corpus does not require one; the 24 terms are five different kinds of thing. H2 status is multidimensional: CONFIRMED. H3 context-dependent status algebra: NOT REQUIRED. H4 status is partly derived: CONFIRMED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Scores the S1611-mandated 4 status hypotheses against S1606's findings: H1 (one canonical set) REFUTED; H2 (multidimensional) CONFIRMED (Sigma-perp-Gamma); H3 (context-dependent algebra) NOT REQUIRED (context lives in the assertion); H4 (partly derived) CONFIRMED (Sigma derives from Assessment, Conflicted derives from state) -- explicitly closing the hypothesis-testing loop the mandate opened.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transition relation Sigma x Event -> Sigma: total and deterministic over three states; Unknown -> Supported on supporting evidence, -> Refuted on contradicting, and back to Unknown on retraction. No artificial exceptions are needed. The six-state historical vocabulary cannot achieve this: Superseded
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes the S1611-mandated status-transition-algebra test: the 3-state Sigma admits a total, deterministic transition relation with no artificial exceptions, while the rejected 6-state historical vocabulary structurally cannot (Superseded and Invalidated have no valid Sigma-transitions since they are a relation and a governance act respectively) -- providing the mathematical (not preference-based) criterion the mandate demanded for choosing between vocabularies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: status transitions follow the covering relation and cannot skip levels. The current corpus says this invariant is witnessed, but also explicitly identifies a missing transition calculus: the ladder tells us which states exist, but not yet what operation moves an item between them. ... a_rows_sample.anchor: ReplayAssertion -- identity is a content hash including time; policy captured externally as a hash; no status field; documented invariant 'once created is immutable... they do NOT mutate.' EvidenceSet -- 'References are opaque strings... this VO holds no transport' (ADR-T16). Evidence by reference,
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds 4 independent corroborations from unrelated production bounded contexts (convergent evolution, not KnowledgeOS-derived): ReplayAssertion uses a content hash (including time) as identity, captures policy externally, has no status field, and is documented immutable -- matching the S1595 identity-repair direction; EvidenceSet holds evidence strictly by reference, never by value (ADR-T16), exactly matching the corpus derivation's rejection of embedding evidence objects; EventProvenance uses (correlationId,causationId), explicitly scoped to Integration Events only; and authorities.yaml documents governance status as independent of lifecycle status, meaning Sigma-perp-Gamma orthogonality (S1606) is enforced in running production configuration by a linter, not merely a theoretical derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the corpus already identifies identity as a governed invariant, while warning that calling the five-dimensional structure an 'Identity Space' would create a semantic collision. The preferred name is therefore Knowledge Dimension Model, with identity treated as a property preserved by separation rath
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a naming correction from newer corpus material: the five-dimensional structure should be called 'Knowledge Dimension Model', not 'Identity Space', to avoid a semantic collision -- identity is a property preserved by separation across the dimensions, not a sixth dimension itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If two different bounded contexts use the same word, do they actually refer to the same domain concept? If not: same word != same concept. The converse is also important: different words != different concepts, because historical evolution may have renamed the same underlying concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central bidirectional DDD test for the vocabulary audit: same word does not imply same concept across bounded contexts, and conversely different words do not imply different concepts, since historical renaming may hide underlying identity -- applied via a word->meaning->bounded-context->type->invariant chain for every term.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preliminary canonical vocabulary map [~29 terms each rated Domain concept/Mechanism/Governance/Ambiguous with a color verdict, e.g. Observation and Evidence green/strong, State and Context and Transformation red/ambiguous]. The classifications above are audit findings, not a final frozen ubiquitous
b_rows_sample.statement: Produces a preliminary classification of ~29 corpus terms into domain-concept/mechanism/governance/ambiguous categories with a strength verdict per term, flagging State, Context, and Transformation as the most ambiguous (red) and Observation, Evidence, Assessment, Determination, Validation, Truth, Belief, Event, Action, Command, Authority, Governance, Conflict, Unknown, Identity, Invariant as comparatively strong (green) -- explicitly an audit finding, not a frozen vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should preserve the integrity of claims, evidence, justification, authority, epistemic standing, uncertainty, conflict, identity and revision. That is materially narrower than generic Information. Information superseteq Knowledge is a plausible conceptual relationship. ... Information sh
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Knowledge as a materially narrower domain concept than generic Information (KnowledgeOS's scope is claims/evidence/justification/authority/standing/uncertainty/conflict/identity/revision), proposing Information superset-or-equal Knowledge as a plausible but not yet set-theoretically formalized relationship, with a firm DDD conclusion that Information must not be used as a synonym for Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WORLD/SOURCES -> OBSERVATION/EVIDENCE -> INTERPRETATION/MODEL/HYPOTHESIS -> CLAIM/ASSERTION -> JUSTIFICATION/ASSESSMENT -> EPISTEMIC STANDING ... explicitly warns not to collapse layers merely because a mechanism can produce them. ... an observation may become evidence, but Observation not-equiv Evi
b_rows_sample.statement: Situates Observation!=Evidence within a full 6-layer architectural pipeline (World/Sources -> Observation/Evidence -> Interpretation/Model/Hypothesis -> Claim/Assertion -> Justification/Assessment -> Epistemic Standing), explicitly warning against collapsing layers just because one mechanism happens to produce several of them in sequence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim / Assertion in the same conceptual layer. But that does not establish identity. Model A: synonyms. Model B: Claim is the proposition being put forward, Assertion is a represented/admitted claim. Model C: different bounded contexts. At present Claim equiv Assertion is not established. This must
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses 3 explicit unresolved models for the Claim-vs-Assertion relationship (synonyms; Claim as proposed vs Assertion as admitted/represented; or genuinely different bounded contexts), concluding none is currently established -- this question remains open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: inference is best treated as a process/mechanism, while determination is a recorded epistemic result. ... Validation is an operation/mechanism. Assessment is its possible output. Validation != Assessment. ... Validation should probably be a domain operation/process, not an entity called Validation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms and DDD-classifies two operation/output pairs: Inference (process, Input->Candidate) is distinct from Determination (recorded result, Assessment->EpistemicStanding); Validation (operation) is distinct from Assessment (its output), matching the earlier transition audit's Validate:KxX->Assessment finding and recommending Validation be modeled as a domain operation, not an entity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: knowledge informs action, but does not execute it. The Decision Boundary contains a DecisionRecord, while the decision itself belongs to the actor. Determination != Decision. Candidate conceptual chain: Assessment -> Determination -> Recommendation -> Decision -> Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Determination!=Decision as a critical boundary (knowledge informs action but does not execute it; a DecisionRecord exists but the decision itself belongs to the actor), proposing a 5-stage conceptual chain Assessment->Determination->Recommendation->Decision->Action, substantially stronger than treating determination and decision as synonyms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion != Truth, Authority != Truth, Confidence != Truth. ... KnowledgeOS therefore should not contain an operation conceptually equivalent to ProveTruth(K). Its domain responsibility is narrower: Assess, Validate, Preserve, Qualify, Record. Truth is not a KnowledgeOS-owned state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a major DDD boundary invariant: Assertion, Authority and Confidence are each distinct from Truth, so KnowledgeOS's domain responsibility is limited to Assess/Validate/Preserve/Qualify/Record, never a ProveTruth(K) operation -- whether truth can ever be internally defined is left as a separate philosophical/mathematical question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: nothing currently justifies Uncertainty = 1 - Confidence or Confidence = P(True|Evidence). That would require a statistical model and probability space. Therefore Confidence, Uncertainty, Belief must remain separate vocabulary until their formal semantics are established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Blocks two specific unjustified numeric identifications (Uncertainty=1-Confidence; Confidence=P(True|Evidence)) absent a fully specified statistical model and probability space, keeping Confidence, Uncertainty, and Belief as separate, formally unresolved vocabulary rather than collapsing them into one numeric concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State currently has at least three meanings: Mathematical state S_t, Knowledge state K_t, Application/system state. These cannot be silently identified. ... State is currently polysemous. I would recommend that the final language use explicit qualifiers: Knowledge State, Epistemic State, Application
b_rows_sample.statement: Names State the most dangerous overloaded word, with at least 3 distinct senses (mathematical S_t, knowledge K_t, application/system runtime state) that must not be silently identified; recommends explicit qualified terms (Knowledge State, Epistemic State, Application State, System State) as the fix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DomainEvent != EventMessage unless explicitly mapped. The earlier formulation Event -> Delta K is therefore a domain-level proposition, not automatically an implementation statement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes DomainEvent (a meaningful domain occurrence) from EventMessage (a technical/implementation messaging mechanism), concluding the corpus formulation Event->DeltaK is a domain-level proposition that should not be automatically read as an implementation-level statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calling all of them 'Transformation' produces semantic collapse [R for epistemic reasoning, delta for event/state transition, tau for context-contract transition, T for abstract state evolution]. ... Reserve Transformation as a mathematical umbrella only. Use more precise DDD names: Assess, Validate
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Transformation as the most problematic overloaded term (already shown in Step 251 to cover 4 distinct functions R/delta/tau/T), recommending it be reserved only as a mathematical umbrella label while 8 more precise DDD operation names (Assess, Validate, Determine, Revise, Admit, Supersede, Apply Event, Transition Knowledge State) replace it in domain language -- explicitly a naming recommendation, not established vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Command = request while Action = execution. Command != Action ... KnowledgeOS should not automatically turn a command into an action. ... Policy = normative rule while Governance = mechanism/process for applying and enforcing normative rules. Policy != Governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes two further non-collapses: Command (request) != Action (execution), with the constraint that KnowledgeOS must not automatically convert a command into an action; and Policy (normative rule) != Governance (the mechanism/process applying and enforcing rules), consistent with the constitutional architecture treating governance as a boundary condition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: an AuthorityGrant, representing a recorded human act assigning authority, and explicitly states that evidence, assessment and source do not self-authorize. Authority != EvidenceQuality and Authority != Truth. This is one of the strongest surviving ubiquitous-language definitions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Authority via an explicit AuthorityGrant entity (a recorded human act assigning authority), establishing that evidence, assessment and source never self-authorize -- Authority is independent of both evidence quality and truth, named one of the strongest surviving ubiquitous-language results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Context is currently overloaded between: bounded context; operational context; reasoning context; transition context; governance context; mathematical parameter/context C. ... C has been used as a mathematical symbol while Context also means a DDD bounded context. C != automatically BoundedContext.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Context as overloaded across 6 distinct senses (DDD bounded context, operational, reasoning, transition, governance, and the mathematical symbol C), specifically warning that the mathematical parameter C must not be automatically conflated with the DDD notion of a 'bounded context' -- flagged as needing an explicit later fix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance = origin/support of an artifact while Lineage = evolution/derivation history. ... the exact formal relationship remains OPEN. ... Conflict != Rejection. A conflict represents competing/incompatible epistemic material. Rejection represents an assessment/decision concerning admissibility or
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate Provenance (artifact origin/support) vs Lineage (evolution/derivation history) distinction with a worked example, while leaving their exact formal relationship OPEN; separately confirms Conflict != Rejection (competing epistemic material vs an admissibility/standing decision) as an established corpus non-collapse with the consequence Conflict->Assessment may occur but Conflict=Rejected is wrong.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown != False. This means Unknown should be modeled as an epistemic status, not as a Boolean negative. ... Identity != Representation and Identity != Dimension. ... Identity(K_t) = Identity(K_{t+1}) under revision? The corpus still records this as unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Unknown!=False (epistemic status, not Boolean negative) and Identity!=Representation / Identity!=Dimension as strong vocabulary anchors, while leaving genuinely open whether an object's identity is preserved across revision (Identity(K_t)=Identity(K_{t+1})?), recorded elsewhere in the corpus as unresolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a mathematically elegant tuple can be semantically ill-typed before it is mathematically ill-typed. For example C may mean Context [4 senses] ... A may mean Authority; Assessment; Action; Assertion. ... Every mathematical symbol must have exactly one declared semantic type within its scope. ... This
b_rows_sample.statement: States the step's most consequential general finding: a mathematically elegant kernel tuple like K=(K,C,T,E,A) can be semantically ill-typed BEFORE it is mathematically ill-typed, since single-letter symbols like C (Context, in >=4 senses) and A (Authority/Assessment/Action/Assertion) are each linguistically overloaded; proposes a semantic-type-discipline rule requiring every mathematical symbol to have exactly one declared semantic type per scope (e.g. E_obs:Observation vs E_ev:Evidence) as a genuine prerequisite for proving any transition function well-typed, not mere notational cosmetics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a preliminary non-collapse set [16 named distinctions including Knowledge Product != Knowledge, KnowledgeOS != Reasoning Engine, Supersession != Deletion, Reasoning != Validation, Model != Reality]. ... one of the most valuable results of Step 252. ... what remains unresolved: [8 named open equaliti
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the audit's results into a 16-item non-collapse set (established architectural invariants, e.g. Knowledge Product!=Knowledge, KnowledgeOS!=Reasoning Engine, Supersession!=Deletion, Reasoning!=Validation, Model!=Reality) called one of the step's most valuable results, alongside an explicit 8-item list of relationships not ready for canonical freezing (most importantly whether EpistemicState is a component of Knowledge State or a separate qualified state).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: We want to know whether there exists a corresponding state transformation T:K x I -> K such that F(That(H,i)) = T(F(H),i) for every valid H and input i. If this holds, then the history dynamics descend to the state space.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the formal question of state sufficiency: given a history space H, a proposed state abstraction F:H->K, and a history-level transformation That:HxI->H, does a corresponding state-level transformation T:KxI->K exist such that F(That(H,i))=T(F(H),i) for all valid H,i -- i.e. do history dynamics descend to the state space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_A ~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B). Then state sufficiency requires: H_A ~_F H_B => That(H_A,i) ~_F That(H_B,i). Thus ~_F must be a congruence with respect to valid transformations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the equivalence relation ~_F induced by the state abstraction (H_A~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B)) and states the central congruence requirement: this equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation for the state representation to be sufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now suppose the proposed state representation retains only Content(K)={p}. ... Authorized(A)=true but Authorized(B)=false. Then F(That(H_A,validate)) != F(That(H_B,validate)). Yet initially F(H_A)=F(H_B). Content-only K fails the congruence test. This is a genuine falsification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a content-only knowledge state via a worked example: two histories with different evidence sources (A authorized, B not) collapse to the same content-only state, but a governance-sensitive validation transformation produces divergent outcomes (Validated vs Unvalidated) depending on the discarded source information -- a genuine congruence failure, showing content-only K is insufficient once authority-sensitive transformations are valid operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose we enrich the state with lambda(e)=source(e). Now F(H_A) != F(H_B) ... The previous counterexample disappears. But this does not yet prove sufficiency. We have only shown one missing distinction has been restored.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows adding a source/provenance field lambda(e)=source(e) to the state resolves the specific counterexample found, but explicitly cautions this only restores one missing distinction and does not establish global sufficiency -- more collapsed-but-behaviorally-different histories must still be searched for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose H_C and H_D have identical Content and Provenance. But H_C was produced under policy pi_1 while H_D was produced under pi_2 ... F(H_C)=F(H_D) under a representation that omits policy history. But T(H_C,i) != T(H_D,i). ... Is Policy part of state, provenance, or external context? ... It is de
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a further counterexample: two histories identical in content and provenance but produced under different policies collapse to the same state under a policy-omitting representation, yet future validation depending on the original governing policy produces different results -- concluding whether policy belongs to state, provenance, or external context cannot be decided by convenience but is determined by transformation sufficiency (independently arriving at a question the parallel verifier track, S1602/S1603, was also attacking).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two histories have the same proposition but different validity intervals theta_A(p)=[t0,t1), theta_B(p)=[t1,t2). Suppose a transformation asks CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)? Then the two states produce different results. ... Temporal validity is not merely decorative metadata if temporal queries are
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-query counterexample (CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)?) that a state representation omitting temporal qualification fails congruence when temporal queries are valid operations -- confirming temporal validity is functionally load-bearing, not decorative metadata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: e1->p and e2->not p. Compare K_A={p,e1} with K_B={p,e1,e2,not p}. A transformation T_assess may produce Assessment(K_A)=Supported but Assessment(K_B)=Conflicted. ... A state representation containing only the latest proposition K={p} would lose information necessary for future assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a contradictory-evidence counterexample showing evidence multiplicity is semantically relevant: two states differing only in whether conflicting evidence is retained produce different Assessment outcomes (Supported vs Conflicted) under T_assess, so a state keeping only the latest proposition would lose information needed for future assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose an information component x can affect the result of a valid future transformation T(K,i). Then x cannot be discarded from the state abstraction unless it is recoverable from other state information. Formally: x is semantically disposable => x=f(K) for some reconstruction function f, or no va
a_rows_sample.statement: States a general disposability criterion generalizing all the preceding counterexamples: an information component x may be discarded from the state abstraction only if it is reconstructible from the remaining state (x=f(K) for some f) or no valid operation can distinguish states differing only in x -- giving a formal test for classifying any candidate field as state, metadata, provenance, external context, or truly redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=F(H) is a transformation-sufficient representation if all permitted future semantics can be determined from K, rather than the complete H. But we should not call K a sufficient statistic without qualification. ... K must be sufficient for the permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit but qualified analogy to the statistical notion of a sufficient statistic: a state K=F(H) is transformation-sufficient if all permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics can be determined from K rather than the full history H -- but the file cautions the statistical term applies to a specific model/parameter and should not be borrowed unqualified, since the KnowledgeOS requirement is broader (sufficiency for a whole permitted transformation semantics, not one parameter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H ~ mu_H. Then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K = F_* mu_H. ... mu_K is a regime-level object, not necessarily part of K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the state abstraction to measure theory without making it foundational: if H is a random history with distribution mu_H, then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K=F_*mu_H (mu_K(A)=mu_H(F^{-1}(A)) for measurable A); explicitly classifies mu_K as a regime-level object, consistent with the parallel Step 246 finding (S1601) that probability belongs to a regime projection, not to K itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F is a compression map. The question becomes: Is this compression lossless with respect to the semantics we care about? That is exactly the congruence question. ... F o That = T o F. This is the formal expression of state sufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the commutative-diagram criterion F o That = T o F as the formal expression of state sufficiency (the state abstraction F is a compression map; sufficiency means the compression is lossless with respect to the transformation semantics), calling it one of the strongest formal tests obtained in the corpus so far, and gives the corresponding failure interpretation (a non-commuting diagram means the proposed state representation has lost necessary information).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(Content,Qualification,Governance) survives the experiments only if those components contain all information required by valid transformations. ... we should not yet assert K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as a final decomposition. Instead: K must be defined by transformation sufficiency. This reverses
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the design question from 'what fields should a Knowledge State have?' to 'what information must a state preserve so that all valid KnowledgeOS transformations remain well-defined?'; explicitly withholds asserting K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as final until it survives transformation-sufficiency testing -- a route to the same skepticism about the 5-tuple that the parallel verifier track reached by counterexample.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimality = systematic removal + congruence testing. This is far stronger than selecting the smallest-looking tuple. ... Minimality is always relative to the transformation language. ... Minimality(K) = Minimality(K | T). There may be no context-free 'minimal Knowledge State.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates minimality testing as systematic per-component removal followed by re-checking the congruence criterion (F^{-i} o That = T^{-i} o F^{-i}), rather than choosing the smallest-looking tuple by inspection; states the important architectural corollary that minimality is always relative to the transformation language T (Minimality(K)=Minimality(K|T)) -- there may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State, since a richer future transformation set can make previously-discardable information necessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition: T:K x I -> K is semantically well-defined with respect to That iff F(H1)=F(H2) => F(That(H1,i))=F(That(H2,i)) for all valid H1,H2,i. Equivalently F o That = T o F. ... not yet a proven KnowledgeOS theorem, because the full transformation set has not been estab
a_rows_sample.statement: States the phase's central named proposition (Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition), giving a single precise, computationally testable mathematical criterion for when a state-level transformation is semantically well-defined relative to a history-level one -- explicitly labeled not yet a proven theorem because the full KnowledgeOS transformation set has not itself been established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PASS -- Transformation congruence criterion established. FAIL -- Global state sufficiency not yet demonstrated. OPEN -- Minimal sufficient Knowledge State. ... K should not be defined independently of T. Instead, the pair (K,T) must be reconstructed together.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the Step-248 verdict: PASS on establishing the congruence criterion; FAIL on demonstrating global state sufficiency; OPEN on minimal sufficient K; states the phase's major conceptual shift -- K must not be designed independently of the transformation set T, but the pair (K,T) must be reconstructed jointly -- and sets Step 249 as Transformation Algebra Reconstruction, to derive the corpus-supported transformation classes (T_create, T_observe, T_infer, T_validate, T_revise, T_reject, T_merge, T_supersede, ...) with domain/codomain/preconditions/postconditions/invariants/composability for each.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can two states with identical current representation produce different valid future behavior? ... If T(K_A)=K'_A and T(K_B)=K'_B with K'_A not equiv K'_B, then history affects future semantics. In that case, the compressed state K is not sufficient. This gives us a rigorous state sufficiency criteri
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the provenance-metadata-vs-constitutive question into a testable future-behavior criterion avoiding philosophical argument: if two states with identical current representation but different history produce different results under the same transformation, then the state representation is insufficient -- directly the criterion S1608 (Step 248) then executes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose they produce identical lineage edges. Yet the transformations had different policies pi_A != pi_B. If policy is semantically relevant, then lambda_A=lambda_B does not imply H_A = H_B. ... Potentially lambda=(source,transformation,actor,time,policy,evidence). But this is again a candidate str
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies plain parent-child lineage as a sufficient history compression: two histories can produce identical lineage edges while having been governed by different policies, so if policy is semantically relevant then lineage-equality does not imply history-equivalence -- proposing a richer candidate lambda=(source,transformation,actor,time,policy,evidence), still only a candidate structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That requires: H_1 ~_H H_2 => T(H_1) ~_H T(H_2). This is a congruence condition. If it holds, the transformation descends from histories to states. ... State abstraction is valid only if it is transformation-compatible.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the congruence condition required for the equivalence-class definition of Knowledge State to be usable: ~_H must be preserved by every valid transformation (H1~_H H2 => T(H1)~_H T(H2)), so that transformations descend consistently from histories to their equivalence classes -- directly foreshadowing S1608's F o That = T o F criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest mathematical structure that satisfies all non-negotiable requirements? Construct a sequence K0 -> K1 -> K2 -> ... where each added component must have a demonstrated necessity. ... The final result must distinguish MINIMALITY PROVEN from MINIMALITY PLAUSIBLE from MINIMALITY NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a 'minimal adequate K' procedure: build up a sequence K0->K1->K2->... adding only demonstrably-necessary components (tested against 7 questions per candidate: forcing requirement, external representability, derivability, removal breakage, reconstructability, circularity, unwanted coupling), and introduces a 3-level minimality-confidence taxonomy (PROVEN / PLAUSIBLE / NOT ESTABLISHED) explicitly rejecting fewer-fields as a minimality argument -- complementing S1608's congruence-based removal test with a positive constructive procedure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot yet remove Merge, Supersede, Split, Withdraw because the corpus may require them for capabilities that have not yet been tested. Therefore the minimality status is: NOT YET TESTABLE rather than: minimal set found.
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares minimality of the state-changing operation family NOT YET TESTABLE (not merely unresolved), since Merge/Supersede/Split/Withdraw cannot yet be safely removed given untested capability requirements -- consistent with S1608's mandate that minimality testing requires actual removal-and-congruence checks, not inspection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We need to distinguish three claims: Representable, Derivable, Primitive. They are not equivalent. If X=f(T) then X may be derivable. But that does not establish that X is unnecessary. Conversely, if X can be encoded inside T, that does not prove that the semantic concept represented by X can be eli
b_rows_sample.statement: States a 3-way non-equivalence governing the whole removal-test methodology: Representable, Derivable, and Primitive are distinct claims, so encoding X inside another structure T neither proves X is unnecessary nor eliminates the semantic concept it represents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A component is removable only if there exists a reconstruction function r_i: K^-i -> K such that all required semantics are preserved. For every valid operation T, we require a commuting condition: r_i o T^-i = T o r_i. ... This is the formal version of the state-sufficiency criterion already develo
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the component-removal criterion as a commuting-diagram condition (r_i o T^-i = T o r_i for a reconstruction function r_i), explicitly identified as the same state-sufficiency congruence criterion developed in Step 248 (S1608), now applied component-wise rather than to the whole state abstraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Minimality(K|T) not Minimality(K). ... if T2 superset T1 adds Merge, Supersede, Replay, ConflictResolution and provenance-sensitive operations, the same representation may cease to be sufficient. ... There may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms and applies Step 248's transformation-relative minimality principle (Minimality(K|T), not Minimality(K)) as the governing frame for the Step-254 removal tests, since expanding the transformation set can make a previously-sufficient representation insufficient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T mentioning K =/=> K derivable from T. Verdict: K is NOT shown removable. But importantly: K is also NOT proven primitive. ... C cannot currently be removed. But again: C is not thereby proven primitive. Context appears semantically necessary to some formulations, but its formal type remains unreso
b_rows_sample.statement: Executes removal tests on K and C from the Step-230 kernel (K,C,T,E,A): K appearing inside T's signature does not prove K is derivable from T, so K is neither shown removable nor proven primitive; Context similarly cannot currently be removed (no established C=f(K,T,E,A) function, and any generic projection would silently pick one of Context's several overloaded meanings) but is also not thereby proven primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At t=0, external evidence may exist before any transformation occurs. Therefore Evidence_0 cannot generally be reconstructed from History(T) alone. This is structurally analogous to the provenance failure. Verdict: Evidence cannot presently be shown removable. ... there is no valid general function
b_rows_sample.statement: Executes removal tests on Evidence and Authority: initial (t=0) external evidence cannot generally be reconstructed from History(T) alone (structurally analogous to the provenance base-case failure), so Evidence is not removable; Authority likewise has no general reconstruction function from the remaining components since it originates from an external actor/governance act (evidence, assessment and source do not self-authorize), so Authority is not removable either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T=f(K,C,E,A) ... The corpus explicitly warns that the theory cannot simultaneously claim T primitive and T=f(K,C,E,A) without specifying the direction of primitiveness. ... T may be primitive OR derived, but the corpus has not chosen. This is not a minor issue. It determines the ontology of the enti
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs the reverse removal test on Transformation T itself, finding the corpus has never chosen a direction for T's primitiveness (T could be primitive, or derived as T=f(K,C,E,A)), and warns this ambiguity is not minor -- it determines the ontology of the entire kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At least four components appear inside the definition/signature of T. ... kernel independence classified as refuted for both Step 230 and Step 232. ... Kernel component count != number of independent primitives. A five-tuple is not automatically a five-primitive ontology.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central negative conclusion of the removal tests: since at least 4 of the 5 K230=(K,C,T,E,A) components appear inside T's own signature, kernel component count is not the same as the number of independent primitives -- a five-tuple candidate kernel is not automatically a five-primitive ontology, confirmed as refuted independence for both Step 230 and Step 232.

b_rows_sample.anchor: History(T)=empty. Yet Provenance(H1) != Provenance(H2). Therefore History(T) cannot reconstruct all provenance. This is already recorded as a formal base-case failure. a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 232's K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) is best understood as a later abstraction over several earlier strands. But the corpus has not yet demonstrated that T_t is a single operation capable of subsuming delta, tau, R, Update, Revise, ... without losing semantics. T_t is currently a synthesis-level abstraction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly demotes Step 232's K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) from historically canonical status to a synthesis-level abstraction over several earlier, semantically distinct strands (delta, tau, R, Update, Revise), since no proof shows T_t can subsume them without semantic loss.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [Reconciliation matrix, 10 rows: Q15 compatible candidate; Q20 unresolved; Step 031 distinct; 025k possible sub-family; Step 049 placeholder; Step 069 unresolved equivalence; Steps 189/203 distinct; Step 204 compatible candidate; Step 205 partially unresolved; Step 232 not yet canonical]
a_rows_sample.statement: Produces the mandated reconciliation matrix across 10 historical transition formulations, each scored on signature, primary layer, relationship to Step 232, and verdict (2 compatible candidates, 3 distinct, 2 unresolved, 1 placeholder, 1 partially unresolved, and Step 232 itself marked not yet canonical) -- deliberately avoiding a single unified verdict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The contradiction appears when these are treated as though they were the same function despite differing: domains; codomains; arities; semantics; failure models; context treatment. ... Transformation remains polysemous.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces the root cause of 'Transformation' polysemy to treating mathematically distinct functions (delta, tau, T, R) as though identical despite differing domains, codomains, arities, semantics, failure models and context treatment -- confirming and explaining the polysemy S1614 flagged as a term-overload problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus map records 7+ formalizations of Knowledge State and explicitly identifies state equality as undefined. Therefore we cannot yet assume K_t = S_t. At most S_t may be a state representation in one layer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces the genealogy of the State symbol itself: the corpus records 7+ distinct formalizations of Knowledge State with state equality left undefined, so K_t=S_t (using two different historical notations interchangeably) cannot be assumed -- S_t may at most be one layer's state representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: evidence equivalence ~ is undefined and whether evidence belongs inside K_t remains unresolved. Therefore a transition delta(K,E) does not yet tell us whether E is: external input; part of K; lineage; provenance; or a separate evidence store.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces Evidence's genealogy across 4 named corpus sources (EXP-01 tuples, Step 031, Q14 structures, Steps 004/005 aggregation), finding evidence equivalence undefined and E's placement relative to K (external input, inside K, lineage, provenance, or separate store) unresolved even within the transition formulation delta(K,E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation != Evidence. This is explicitly ratified in the current non-collapse vocabulary. ... the chain World -Omega-> Observation should not be silently collapsed into World -> Evidence. That distinction matters for the transition genealogy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Observation!=Evidence as an already-ratified corpus non-collapse, and shows it materially affects the transition genealogy since the World->Observation chain (via Omega:W->O) must not be silently treated as equivalent to a World->Evidence chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: status transitions follow the covering relation and cannot skip levels. The current corpus says this invariant is witnessed, but also explicitly identifies a missing transition calculus: the ladder tells us which states exist, but not yet what operation moves an item between them. ... Epistemic stat
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a distinct gap in the epistemic-status ladder (invariant I-12, covering relation, no level-skipping): the corpus defines which epistemic states exist but not the operation that moves an item between them -- an epistemic transition function distinct from, and still missing alongside, the ordinary state transition delta/T.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A state transition may actually contain at least two different transitions: Knowledge-object lifecycle (K -> K') and Epistemic-status transition (e_i -> e_j). ... K_{t+1}=T(K_t) may be too coarse to explain Status_t -> Status_{t+1}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues 'state transition' actually conflates two distinct transitions -- knowledge-object lifecycle (K->K') and epistemic-status transition (e_i->e_j, constrained by the covering relation) -- concluding the abstract K_{t+1}=T(K_t) formulation may be too coarse to explain status evolution on its own.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the different formulations appear to answer different questions [delta, tau, R, Update, E->G->O, K_{t+1}=T(K_t) each answering a distinct question]. Therefore the historical 'inconsistency' may partly be layer conflation, not necessarily theoretical contradiction. But we cannot declare all differenc
a_rows_sample.statement: States the step's central methodological insight: the apparent proliferation of competing transition formulations partly reflects that each answers a genuinely different question (event application, contract-permitted transition, epistemic result of evidence, knowledge revision, federated outcome, abstract state evolution) rather than pure contradiction -- but explicitly refuses to let this insight excuse away the formulations that remain genuinely unresolved competing models rather than merely different layers.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we must explicitly reject these unsupported equations: delta=tau; R=T; Validate=T; Event=Delta-K; K=S; History=Lineage; unless the corpus later provides the necessary definitions and mappings.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists 6 specific unsupported equations to be explicitly rejected pending corpus-provided mappings: delta=tau, R=T, Validate=T, Event=Delta-K, K=S, and History=Lineage -- the last consistent with the S1600/S1603/S1612 finding that provenance and lineage/history are distinct objects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The candidate kernel cannot yet contain merely (K,T). It must at least distinguish State from Transition from Assessment from Decision from Event and History/Lineage. Whether these are all primitives of one final mathematical object is still open. ... Transition System = typed family of related tran
a_rows_sample.statement: States the step's final conclusion and the most important kernel-design consequence: the candidate kernel must distinguish at least 6 roles (State, Transition, Assessment, Decision, Event, History/Lineage) rather than collapsing to (K,T); the strongest current hypothesis is that the Transition System is a typed family of related structures, not one closed algebra, though final mathematical closure remains unproven -- directly aligning with the parallel verifier track's typed-family conclusion (S1603, S1612).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WORLD/SOURCES -> OBSERVATION/EVIDENCE -> INTERPRETATION/MODEL/HYPOTHESIS -> CLAIM/ASSERTION -> JUSTIFICATION/ASSESSMENT -> EPISTEMIC STANDING ... explicitly warns not to collapse layers merely because a mechanism can produce them. ... an observation may become evidence, but Observation not-equiv Evi
a_rows_sample.statement: Situates Observation!=Evidence within a full 6-layer architectural pipeline (World/Sources -> Observation/Evidence -> Interpretation/Model/Hypothesis -> Claim/Assertion -> Justification/Assessment -> Epistemic Standing), explicitly warning against collapsing layers just because one mechanism happens to produce several of them in sequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State currently has at least three meanings: Mathematical state S_t, Knowledge state K_t, Application/system state. These cannot be silently identified. ... State is currently polysemous. I would recommend that the final language use explicit qualifiers: Knowledge State, Epistemic State, Application
a_rows_sample.statement: Names State the most dangerous overloaded word, with at least 3 distinct senses (mathematical S_t, knowledge K_t, application/system runtime state) that must not be silently identified; recommends explicit qualified terms (Knowledge State, Epistemic State, Application State, System State) as the fix.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Calling all of them 'Transformation' produces semantic collapse [R for epistemic reasoning, delta for event/state transition, tau for context-contract transition, T for abstract state evolution]. ... Reserve Transformation as a mathematical umbrella only. Use more precise DDD names: Assess, Validate
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Transformation as the most problematic overloaded term (already shown in Step 251 to cover 4 distinct functions R/delta/tau/T), recommending it be reserved only as a mathematical umbrella label while 8 more precise DDD operation names (Assess, Validate, Determine, Revise, Admit, Supersede, Apply Event, Transition Knowledge State) replace it in domain language -- explicitly a naming recommendation, not established vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add, Remove, Revise, Merge, Split, Supersede, Validate, Reject, Transform. ... What invariants survive these operations?
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 232 (tail) asks whether knowledge states form an algebraic structure under nine operations (Add, Remove, Revise, Merge, Split, Supersede, Validate, Reject, Transform), posing Add(K,x)?, Merge(K1,K2)?, Revise(K,x,x')?, Transform(K_A,C_A,C_B)?, and the key question of what invariants survive these operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathbb K=\{(G,\sigma,\theta,\lambda,\pi)\mid \text{state satisfies the domain invariants}\}. ... (\mathbb K,\mathcal O)
b_rows_sample.statement: The knowledge-state SPACE mathbb K (all admissible states satisfying domain invariants) is distinguished from a particular STATE mathfrak K_t at time t; rather than assuming a classical algebraic structure (ring/field/vector space), the appropriate initial object is a state-transition algebra (mathbb K, mathcal O) where mathcal O is the set of admissible operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation\neq Validation. Validation:\mathbb K\times X\rightarrow Assessment while Transformation:\mathbb K\times Parameters\rightarrow\mathbb K.
b_rows_sample.statement: State-changing vs state-classifying operations: Transformation != Validation -- Validation: mathbb K x X -> Assessment (may merely produce an assessment) while Transformation: mathbb K x Parameters -> mathbb K (changes the state); validation may subsequently trigger a transition, corresponding to the DDD chain Command->Decision->Event->State, rated a much better model than treating CRUD as the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add_x(\mathfrak K) is a partial operation. ... Remove_x:\mathbb K\rightharpoonup\mathbb K. ... Remove(E) may require Reassess(A).
b_rows_sample.statement: Addition Add_x:mathbb K -> mathbb K is a PARTIAL operation, defined only if Invariant(K')=True; Removal Remove_x:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K is likewise partial since an accepted item may depend on the removed one (A-dependsOn->E), so Remove(E) may require Reassess(A).

b_rows_sample.anchor: x_t\xrightarrow{revisedTo}x_{t+1}. Revision=new state+historical relation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revision must not be modeled as overwriting (x_t <- x_{t+1}, destroying history) but as x_t -revisedTo-> x_{t+1}, giving Revision = new state + historical relation, naturally supporting lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \sigma(x_1)=Superseded and \sigma(x_2)=Accepted. Currentness\neq Truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Supersession differs from revision: x1 is retained as historical knowledge marked Superseded (sigma(x1)=Superseded) while x2 is Accepted, again demonstrating Currentness != Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge\neq SetUnion. ... Merge(K_1,K_2,C,P) ... compatible, redundant, complementary, contradictory, superseding. ... TextMerge\neq SemanticMerge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Merge is a partial, semantic operation Merge:mathbb K x mathbb K -|-> mathbb K, not naive set union (Merge != SetUnion) since sources may contain contradictory claims; a proper Merge(K1,K2,C,P) classifies relationships as compatible/redundant/complementary/contradictory/superseding -- giving the DDD principle TextMerge != SemanticMerge (a repository-level/Git merge is not necessarily a domain merge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Split(Merge(K_1,K_2))\neq(K_1,K_2). ... non-invertible knowledge transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Split:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K x mathbb K is not a true mathematical inverse of Merge -- Split(Merge(K1,K2)) != (K1,K2) in general because merge may introduce derived information, reconciliation decisions, normalization, or conflict resolution -- an example of non-invertible knowledge transformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (\mathcal T,\circ) has the structure of a transformation semigroup, assuming closure. ... (\mathcal T,\circ,I) is at least monoid-like. ... We should not claim it yet as a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: The set of admissible transformations mathcal T with composition forms a candidate transformation semigroup (mathcal T, o) assuming closure, with an identity transformation I_K(K)=K making (mathcal T,o,I) at least monoid-like -- explicitly not yet claimed as a proven theorem, but architecturally useful for representing pipelines K3=(T3 o T2 o T1)(K0).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_2\circ T_1 may be mathematically composable but not governance-valid. MathematicalComposition from GovernedComposition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance breaks naive composition: T1 authorized in context C1 composed with T2 (requiring ungranted authority) may be mathematically composable but not governance-valid, requiring MathematicalComposition to be distinguished from GovernedComposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal T_G\subseteq\mathcal T ... T\in\mathcal T_G only if Authority(T)\land Policy(T)\land RequiredEvidence(T). ... we should not automatically call \mathcal T_G a semigroup.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governed transformations mathcal T_G subseteq mathcal T require Authority(T) and Policy(T) and RequiredEvidence(T); mathcal T_G is NOT necessarily closed under composition (T1,T2 in T_G but T2 o T1 not in T_G if the combined transformation crosses a governance boundary) -- an important mathematical correction against assuming T_G is a semigroup.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G(T,K,C,A,P)\in\{0,1\}. K'=T(K) only if G(T,K,C,A,P)=1. ... Evidence is a condition of admissibility, not merely metadata.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance is formalized as a boolean constraint system G(T,K,C,A,P) in {0,1}: a state transition K'=T(K) is valid only if G(T,K,C,A,P)=1, and separately E(T) |= ReqEvidence(T,P) must hold -- evidence is a condition of admissibility, not merely metadata. Together these give the core transition rule K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) subject to G(...)=1 and E_t |= ReqEvidence(T_t,P_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: M_C(\Delta_t)\Rightarrow Governed(T_t). ... U_t=\varnothing. A governed knowledge system may transform information, but material semantic changes may not occur silently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Material-change condition, rated potentially one of the most important invariants in the entire architecture: M_C(Delta_t)=1 (materiality of the diff between K_t and K_{t+1}) implies Governed(T_t); reformulated elegantly as U_t = empty set where U_t is the set of undeclared material changes -- a governed knowledge system may transform information, but material semantic changes may never occur silently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq K_{t+1} ... Clearly not. ... HistoricalKnowledge(K_t)\subseteq HistoricalKnowledge(K_{t+1}). ... HistoricalMonotonicity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is NOT monotonic (K_t subseteq K_{t+1} fails since knowledge can be corrected/withdrawn/superseded/invalidated), but a weaker HistoricalMonotonicity holds: HistoricalKnowledge(K_t) subseteq HistoricalKnowledge(K_{t+1}) -- the system should not erase the fact that a knowledge state existed, even though Current(K_t) need not be monotonic while History(K_<=t) should normally grow.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not assume KnowledgeOS is a lattice. It may become a partial order over particular classes of knowledge states, but this requires proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether knowledge states form a lattice under an information ordering K1<=K2 (K2 contains at least as much accepted information) is explicitly left open and cautioned against assuming, since contradictions complicate a least-upper-bound K1 join K2; likewise no universal statistical information ordering should be assumed given multiple incompatible candidates (entropy, KL divergence, Fisher information, posterior concentration).

b_rows_sample.anchor: F_Y=F_X\circ T^{-1}. ... Y must remain linked to X. This is exactly what lineage is supposed to preserve.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distributional transformation is a rigorous statistical-layer example of knowledge transformation: for X~F and measurable T, Y=T(X) induces F_Y = F_X o T^-1; when KnowledgeOS derives an engineering indicator Y from observed metric X, Y must remain linked to X via provenance/uncertainty/assumptions -- exactly what lineage is meant to preserve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: q_1,q_2\xrightarrow{f}q. ... Validity(q)=g(Validity(q_1),Validity(q_2),f).
b_rows_sample.statement: Derived knowledge q=f(q1,q2) gives a knowledge derivation graph q1,q2-f->q; dependency preservation proposes Validity(q) = g(Validity(q1),Validity(q2),f) so that invalidating q1 makes q suspect -- a candidate for deterministic validity propagation, illustrated by Requirement->ArchitectureDecision->ImplementationConstraint where superseding the Requirement triggers Supersession->ImpactAnalysis on the ArchitectureDecision, not necessarily invalidation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Impact(q)=Descendants(q). ... Reassessment(Impact(q)). This may become one of the most important practical capabilities of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge impact propagation: Impact(q) = Descendants(q) in the provenance/semantic graph, so a material change to q triggers Reassessment(Impact(q)) -- rated potentially one of the most important practical capabilities of KnowledgeOS, and making the transformation algebra explicitly dependency-aware: Input+Context+Evidence+Authority+Dependencies -> Output.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Law 1 -- Traceability ... Law 2 -- Governance ... Law 3 -- Evidence ... Law 4 -- Semantic accountability ... Law 5 -- Historical preservation ... Law 6 -- Epistemic separation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate algebraic laws, rated much closer to architectural invariants than the earlier broad principles: L1 Traceability (exists L(T) for every material transformation), L2 Governance (Material(T)=>Authorized(T)), L3 Evidence (RequiredEvidence(T)=>Evidence(T)), L4 Semantic accountability (MaterialSemanticChange(T)=>Declared(T)), L5 Historical preservation (historical state not silently destroyed), L6 Epistemic separation (Status(q) != Content(q)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: All changes require human approval is a policy. It is not necessarily a universal architectural invariant. ... Every consequential transformation requires an authority mechanism appropriate to its risk and policy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Crucial distinction between invariant and policy: 'all changes require human approval' is a policy, not a universal invariant; the more general, robust invariant is 'every consequential transformation requires an authority mechanism appropriate to its risk and policy' (human approval, delegated authority, deterministic policy, or automated rule).
